title: Data Engineer AWS - Recrutement international (Montréal)
Software Engineer - Red Team
description:
About the AI Security Institute

The AI Security Institute is the world's largest and best-funded team dedicated to understanding advanced AI risks and translating that knowledge into action. We’re in the heart of the UK government with direct lines to No. 10 (the Prime Minister's office), and we work with frontier developers and governments globally.

We’re here because governments are critical for advanced AI going well, and UK AISI is uniquely positioned to mobilise them. With our resources, unique agility and international influence, this is the best place to shape both AI development and government action.

The deadline for applying to this role is Tuesday 8th December, end of day, anywhere on Earth 

About the team 

The Red Team conducts cutting-edge research to identify, evaluate and stress test vulnerabilities in frontier AI systems, sharing our findings directly with leading AI companies, UK officials and allied governments. Our work shapes how the most powerful AI systems are deployed - you can read about it in the The New York Times , The Economist, and The Telegraph . Demand for this work is growing faster than we can currently meet - we're scaling to address that gap. 

The Red Team’s work is crucial to ensuring advanced AI systems are developed and deployed safely. We are composed of three specialised sub-teams: 

- Misuse : stress-testing and jailbreaking safeguards against misuse of dangerous capabilities (e.g. our safeguard testing with Anthropic and OpenAI, and recent work on Boundary Point Jailbreaking , attacks on layered safeguard systems and principles for evaluating misuse safeguards ) 

- Alignment : detecting and understanding misalignment and loss-of-control risks (e.g., our evaluation of GPT-6 Astra , and our research into cheating behaviour in frontier model evaluations ) 

- Control : stress-testing measures that identify and prevent agents taking harmful actions 

While each team has its own focus, we share methodologies, infrastructure and tooling across the wider team. 

Role Description 

We are looking for motivated and talented Software Engineers to join the Red Team. We are seeking exceptional candidates at all experience levels, from junior through to senior, staff and principal levels. 

We are particularly interested in candidates who: 

- Have worked closely with research teams, understanding their needs, building tools they want to use, and automating their workflows. 

- Have a good understanding of frontier AI capabilities, limitations, and risks and how they can be leveraged for automation at scale. 

- Have built infrastructure that works at scale, with a high bar for security. 

- Have experience with serving and training models.

What you’ll be doing 

As a software engineer on one of our sub teams, you might: 

- Build and maintain systems for running red-teaming against frontier models at scale, such as automated jailbreaking pipelines, alignment auditor agents in Inspect Petri, and attacker agents for control red-teaming 

- Design and implement systems for running large scale automated research and engineering with many agents on AISI’s research platform 

- Extend our evaluation tooling, built on Inspect (AISI's open-source framework for evaluating AI), to new kinds of targets 

- Develop novel solutions to performance, reliability, and security problems that arise from running thousands of agents in parallel 

- Work with Core Technology to share infrastructure and avoid duplicating work 

- Help run pre-release testing of frontier models, often to tight deadlines 

- Debug problems as they come up and make sure results are reliable and reproducible 

- Turn loosely defined research ideas into well-tested, documented and maintainable code 

- Review code, share knowledge and help researchers write better software 

Person specification 

You may be a good fit if you have some of the following skills, experience and attitudes: 

- Writing production quality code at fast pace. 

- Interest in developing ways to automate work with agents, while accounting for their limitations. 

- Designing, shipping, and maintaining complex tech products. 

- Improving technical standards across a team, through mentoring and feedback. 

- Strong written and verbal communication skills. 

- Collaborating effectively with many people, including external teams. 

- Experience working with a world-class research team comprised of both scientists and engineers (e.g. in a top-3 lab). 

- Python experience 

- Experience building and maintaining systems on AWS or other cloud providers using infrastructure-as-code. 

Highly Desirable 

We additionally may factor in experience with particular areas like: 

- Expertise in Cloud Infrastructure or Dev Ops (AWS, Azure, Kubernetes, Terraform, CDK, Docker, etc.) 

- Cybersecurity expertise 

- ML Ops (vLLM, agent frameworks, fine-tuning, RAG systems, etc.) 

- Experience with red teaming, adversarial machine learning, or offensive or adversarial security (for example penetration testing or capture-the-flag competitions) 

- Hands-on experience with large language model APIs and the tools around them, such as OpenAI-compatible APIs, agent frameworks or vLLM 

- Building, running or analysing AI evaluations, ideally with Inspect 

- Cloud infrastructure and DevOps experience with AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform or similar 

- Familiarity with how AI could be misused or could slip out of human control, and how safeguards try to prevent this 

This might not be the role for you if:

- You prefer working on production-grade software and would find rapid prototyping or "good enough for now" code frustrating

- You prefer well-defined requirements and long planning cycles. Our priorities shift as new models are released, and our projects often run to tight deadlines. 

Selection process 

The interview process may vary from candidate to candidate, however, you should expect a typical process to include some technical proficiency tests, discussions with a cross-section of our team at AISI (including non-technical staff) and conversations with your team lead. The process will culminate in a conversation with members of the senior leadership team here at AISI.       

Candidates should expect to go through  some or all of the following stages once an application has been submitted:       

- Initial assessment    

- Initial screening call      

- Technical assessment  

- Behavioural interview    

- Final interview with members of the senior leadership team

What We Offer 

Impact you couldn't have anywhere else 

- Incredibly talented, mission-driven and supportive colleagues. 

- Direct influence on how frontier AI is governed and deployed globally. 

- Work with the Prime Minister’s AI Advisor and leading AI companies. 

- Opportunity to shape the first & best-resourced public-interest research team focused on AI security. 

Resources & access 

- Pre-release access to multiple frontier models and ample compute. 

- Extensive operational support so you can focus on research and ship quickly. 

- Work with experts across national security, policy, AI research and adjacent sciences. 

Growth & autonomy 

- If you’re talented and driven, you’ll own important problems early. 

- 5 days off and annual stipends for learning and development, and funding for conferences and external collaborations. 

- Freedom to pursue research bets without product pressure. 

- Opportunities to publish and collaborate externally. 

Life & family* 

- Modern central London office, or where applicable, option to work in similar government offices in Birmingham, Cardiff, Darlington, Edinburgh, Salford or Bristol. 

- Hybrid working, flexibility for occasional remote work abroad and stipends for work-from-home equipment. 

- At least 25 days’ annual leave, 8 public holidays, extra team-wide breaks and 3 days off for volunteering. 

- Generous paid parental leave (36 weeks of UK statutory leave shared between parents + 3 extra paid weeks + option for additional unpaid time). 

- Excellent pension provision, with a choice between Partnership (no employee contributions required and up to 14.75% employer contributions) or Alpha, a valuable defined benefit scheme that provides a guaranteed, inflation-linked retirement income for life. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window). 

- Discounts and benefits for cycling to work, donations and retail/gyms. 

*These benefits apply to direct employees. Benefits may differ for individuals joining through other employment arrangements such as secondments. 

Salary 

Annual salary is benchmarked to role scope and relevant experience. Most offers land between £65,000 and £145,000 made up of a base salary plus a technical allowance (take-home salary = base + technical allowance). 

This role sits outside of the DDaT pay framework given the scope of this role requires in depth technical expertise in frontier AI safety, robustness and advanced AI architectures. 

The full range of salaries are available below: 

- Level 3: £65,000–£75,000 (Base £40,850 + Technical Allowance £24,150–£34,150)

- Level 4: £85,000–£95,000 (Base £48,540 + Technical Allowance £36,460–£46,460)

- Level 5: £105,000–£115,000 (Base £63,165 + Technical Allowance £41,835–£51,835)

- Level 6: £125,000–£135,000 (Base £76,475 + Technical Allowance £48,525–£58,525)

- Level 7: £145,000 (Base £76,475 + Technical Allowance £68,525)

Additional Information

Use of AI in Applications 

Artificial Intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Use of AI tools in recruitment 

We may use AI tools to help our hiring team review applications, for example by summarising application materials and helping us prioritise them against the published criteria. We do not use AI tools to find information about you from other sources, including online. People make every decision. We do not make solely automated decisions about candidates. Find out more, including your rights, in our recruitment privacy notice: https://www.aisi.gov.uk/careers/privacy-policy.

Internal Fraud Database 

The Internal Fraud function of the Fraud, Error, Debt and Grants Function at the Cabinet Office processes details of civil servants who have been dismissed for committing internal fraud, or who would have been dismissed had they not resigned. The Cabinet Office receives the details from participating government organisations of civil servants who have been dismissed, or who would have been dismissed had they not resigned, for internal fraud. In instances such as this, civil servants are then banned for 5 years from further employment in the civil service. The Cabinet Office then processes this data and discloses a limited dataset back to DLUHC as a participating government organisations. DLUHC then carry out the pre employment checks so as to detect instances where known fraudsters are attempting to reapply for roles in the civil service. In this way, the policy is ensured and the repetition of internal fraud is prevented. For more information please see - Internal Fraud Register. 

Security 

Successful candidates must undergo a criminal record check and get baseline personnel security standard (BPSS) clearance before they can be appointed. Additionally, there is a strong preference for eligibility for counter-terrorist check (CTC) clearance . Some roles may require higher levels of clearance, and we will state this by exception in the job advertisement. See our vetti

title: Applied AI Engineer - AI Finance Agent
description:
About BJAK 

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role 

We are looking for applied AI engineers to build AI-native systems for BJAK's AI Finance Agent.

This is not a research-only role. We need builders who can use AI to automate real workflows, improve products, reduce manual work and make financial services easier for users and teams.

What You'll Own 

- 
Build AI-powered workflows, assistants, agents and automation systems.

- 
Apply AI across customer support, CRM, onboarding, claims, renewals, payments, operations and internal tools.

- 
Work with product and engineering teams to turn manual processes into scalable AI-native systems.

- 
Build integrations with LLMs, internal data, APIs, documents, knowledge bases and business systems.

- 
Design evaluation, monitoring and fallback flows so AI outputs are useful, safe and reliable.

- 
Prototype quickly, test with users or operators, then productionize what works.

- 
Improve speed, quality and consistency across workflows using AI where it creates real business value.

What We're Looking For 

- 
Strong software engineering foundation, preferably with Python and backend systems.

- 
Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs, agents, RAG, workflow automation or AI tools.

- 
Able to connect AI systems with real product, data and operational workflows.

- 
Good judgement on where AI helps and where rule-based systems or human review are better.

- 
Understands evaluation, accuracy, latency, cost, privacy and failure modes.

- 
Fast builder who can prototype, test and ship practical systems.

- 
Experience in fintech, insurance, support automation, CRM or operations automation is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want 

- 
Practical AI builder, not just a prompt experimenter.

- 
Thinks in workflows, systems and measurable quality.

- 
Can build quickly but still cares about guardrails and reliability.

- 
Comfortable working with messy real-world data and processes.

- 
Honest about what AI can and cannot do.

This Role Is Not For 

- 
People who only want research projects with no production ownership.

- 
Candidates who treat AI as demos instead of working systems.

- 
Engineers who do not care about evaluation, reliability or user impact.

- 
People who overclaim AI impact without evidence.

- 
Builders who cannot work with product, ops and business teams.

Location 

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Netherlands . We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Netherlands. 

Language 

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process 

Our process is designed to move fast:

- 
Online assessment or practical task

- 
Technical interview

- 
CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Software Engineer - Delta Platform
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 

About the role

Delta builds BLP’s core software: the technical foundation that everything else at the company runs on.

Who we're looking for

Modelling logic and correctness by construction is paramount to us. We aim to express what must be true, prevent invalid states, and keep systems pristine even as they grow.

Thus, we’re looking for highly ambitious engineers who can tackle difficult problems and think precisely. You must be able to make assumptions explicit and use formal, structured reasoning to reach a solution, and explain why it is correct. Typically, strong background in mathematics is a key foundation for this kind of work. We also place a high value on thoroughness and perfectionism.

Tooling wise, we rely heavily on type systems & functional programming.

What you'll do

Our work spans four areas, you will usually work on a given project within one of:

- Infrastructure: Build and operate the cloud infrastructure BLP depends on, covering security, observability and CI/CD.

- Backend: Develop a large codebase, tackling performance, concurrency and the challenges of distributed systems.

- ML: Apply the latest AI technology to complex, real-world business problems and turn it into reliable production software.

- Unbound: Build our product extension platform, enabling BLP to automate arbitrary customer business processes as we scale.

What you'll bring

We do not require experience with any particular technology or even industry software development experience.

You should, however, provide clear evidence of the abilities we’re looking for. That evidence could include:

- strong academic backgrounds (math PhD/MSc or significant olympiad achievements)

- startup experience (early employee, built productive systems yourself & know what it takes to maintain them)

- FP experience (have deep understanding of programming languages and are able to discern the various tradeoffs of different paradigms)

Flexibility. Work on-site in Zurich or remotely within Europe.

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers .

title: Research Lead, Evaluations
description:
About Black Forest Labs 

We’re the team building the foundational layer for visual intelligence: multimodal models trained jointly on images, video, audio, and action to see, generate, and understand the world.

Our founding team pioneered latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion, the breakthroughs that made generative AI accessible to millions. With FLUX, we're pushing into generative media at scale, machines that act in the physical world, and emerging applications in computer use.

Our FLUX models top public benchmarks and run in production in some of the world's biggest platforms. We're a small, fast growing research lab competing with the largest companies in the world. From our labs in Freiburg to San Francisco, we're building what comes next.

Why This Role 

BFL’s research organization is split into different focus areas, such as pre-training, post-training, reinforcement learning, data, representation learning, evaluations and more. During the day to day work, researchers from these different focus areas work together to solve exciting and hard problems towards solving visual intelligence.

Having the right means to measure what matters is the central starting point for every research project. Researchers make decisions based on the outcomes of evaluations. The right decision can only be made if an evaluation is precise and accurate. As the Evaluations Lead you’re the core driver to ensure that. Central responsibilities include building our eval roadmap in collaboration with the research and product teams, managing and extending our evaluation team, and cross-functional work with project leads to make sure each research project has the best evaluation toolbox to help the people working on it to make the right decisions. Finally, you’re responsible for growing the people in your team and maintain an eye on their long term development during the daily project work.

What You’ll Work On 

- Defining what we evaluate: You are the core driver to create, maintain and extend our evaluations roadmap by collaborating with the product and other research leads who provide the required input.

- Defining how we evaluate: You’ll work with the team to implement our evals roadmap. This includes building new evals. Both benchmarks and the necessary objective functions, involving both automated, AI-based, and human evaluations.

- Minimizing noise in our eval pipeline: Developing frontier AI system requires the most accurate means to measure what matters! You will ensure that results are reproducible and trustworthy, that we understand the error bars behind them and that we measure what we want to measure.

- Understanding what we cannot measure: You’re responsible for highlighting and clearly communicate limitations of each individual evaluation and you will support our project teams to ensure that their chosen set of evaluations has no blind spots in when combined. ****

- Observing training runs and visualizing important findings: You will help with monitoring our most critical training runs from an independent standpoint to ensure that regressions and emerging capabilities are caught early and are clearly communicated.

- Managing our evals team: Your role is a hands-on management role - you’re responsible for growing the team and the people in it. You will define our hiring roadmap and make sure that each team member can grow within BFL, both in terms of their technical skillset and their career.

What We’re Looking For 

- Proven eval experience: You’ve previously designed, run and maintained large and complex evaluation suites for frontier AI systems, involving various kinds of evaluation methods involving both human and automated (both with or without AI) approaches.

- Strong research background: You should have proven experience of designing and implementing evaluations for AI research. Strong understanding of Python is required. A strong understanding of agentic coding is a must.

- Experience as a people manager: One of your core responsibilities will be to grow the team and its members. Understanding what it means to lead a team and how it’s different from an IC role is a must. You should have actively managed a team for at least one year.

- Strong understanding in statistics and good judgement about numbers: You should be familiar with variance, confidence intervals and significance testing. You should be able to identify and resolve situations when blindly trusting numbers leads to wrong conclusions.

- Excellent communication skills: You will have to communicate results with project leads and research leadership. Understanding how to communicate these results and what they don’t tell us is important since they’re the foundation for important decisions.

- First principles thinking: Crafting evaluations for new capabilities is not straightforward. You need to be able to derive new evals which requires proficiency in thinking from first principles

- Prior experience in visual multimodal AI systems is a plus: Ideally you should bring experience in evaluating visual AI systems. Being familiar with additional modalities (audio, language/code, action prediction) for both generation and understanding/detection will be helpful.

How We Work Together 

We’re a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. This role is based in Freiburg, and you’ll join us in the office at least 2 days a week, or one full week every other week.

Everything we do is grounded in four values: 

- Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.

- Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.

- Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

- Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.

If this sounds like work you’d enjoy, we’d love to hear from you.

Compensation 

EUR255K- 295K + equity, depending on profile

Note: We may use AI-assisted tools to help organize applications. All hiring decisions are always made by our team.

title: Applied AI Software Engineer - Defense
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the role

Join Mistral AI’s Defense team to build software for defense institutions and industry.

We are looking for an experienced software engineer with strong engineering fundamentals and a background in data engineering or transactional, analytical or distributed systems. You will help shape the architecture, write production code and own substantial software components, from design through deployment and operation.

This role offers the scope and autonomy of a senior technical individual contributor in a small team. It is particularly suited to engineers operating at Senior or Staff level in demanding product engineering environments who want broad ownership and to stay deeply involved in implementation.

What you will do

- Design and build services for data ingestion, transformation, storage, querying and operational workflows.

- Develop shared data models, APIs and SDKs that help engineers build applications on a consistent foundation.

- Make authorization a core part of the architecture: define and enforce which users, applications and agents can access data or perform actions, with clear audit trails.

- Solve problems involving data consistency, schema evolution, concurrency, performance and failure recovery across services and data systems.

- Turn needs from our applied engineers and defense users into reusable software capabilities, making pragmatic choices about what to build and how to evolve them.

- Own delivery end to end, including implementation, testing, observability, debugging and maintainability in demanding deployment environments.

- Use AI coding tools and coding agents extensively to accelerate implementation, testing, refactoring and debugging. Help the team improve these workflows while maintaining a high engineering standard.

What we are looking for

- Strong practical familiarity with AI coding tools and agentic engineering workflows. You use coding agents regularly, can break complex work into well-scoped tasks, provide effective context, review generated code and validate the result through tests and debugging. You remain accountable for the architecture, correctness, security and maintainability of what you ship.

- A strong track record of building and operating production software, with substantial ownership of complex systems.

title: Developer Experience Engineer - AI SDLC
description:
We Are Sparta 

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

The role

You lead how Sparta builds software in the AI era. You own our AI-native software development lifecycle: the development agents engineers work alongside, the CI/CD that ships their code, and the testing strategy that lets us move fast without breaking trading workflows.

AI has changed how code gets written, reviewed, and tested, and the tooling has not caught up. Your job is to make an engineer with Claude Code, a good harness and a fast pipeline several times more effective, and to prove it with data, not anecdotes.

What you will do

- Own the AI development toolchain. Set up and evolve Claude Code and other development agents across engineering: shared skills, MCP servers, repo context, and guardrails, so agents work well in our codebase out of the box.

- Build agents into the lifecycle. Automate the work around the code: AI-assisted code review, test generation, dependency upgrades, migrations and incident triage, with humans in the loop where it matters.

- Make CI/CD fast and boring. Own build, test and release pipelines across the Nx monorepo: caching, affected-only builds, preview environments and safe, frequent deploys to AWS.

- Build the guardrails for everyone who builds. Anyone can build now, including product, design, data and domain experts working with agents. Create the tooling that makes it safe for them to contribute code: automated quality gates, code ownership and review rules, preview environments, policy checks and agent evals in the pipeline, so good changes ship fast and risky ones are caught early. Testing strategy sits inside this: define what we test at each level and make the right tests cheap to write.

- Keep it secure. Secrets, permissions and sandboxing for agents that read code and run commands, and supply-chain checks in the pipeline.

- Raise the bar for everyone. Run enablement, write the playbooks, pair with teams and turn good practice from one team into the default for all of engineering.

What you bring

- Extensive experience as a hands-on software engineer, with recent focus on developer experience, platform or build and release engineering.

- You have rolled out AI coding tools to a team and made them stick: you know where agents help, where they fail and how to set them up for a real codebase.

- You lead without needing authority: you treat engineers as customers, listen first, and win adoption with tools people want to use.

Nice to have

- Built Claude Code skills, plugins or MCP servers, or extended another agent harness.

- Deep CI/CD experience: you have designed pipelines for a monorepo, cut build and test times, and run safe, frequent releases.

- Infrastructure as code and container platforms.

- Experience defining or running engineering metrics.

Our stack for this team

Claude Ecosystem · Nx monorepo · GitHub · AWS · TypeScript · Python · Kotlin

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable 

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning. 

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission 

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not. 

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem 

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to. 

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you. 

If it's on you, it's in your control. 

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift 

Honesty is an expression of care. 

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

Sparta Commodities is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and promotes diversity within its workforce. We are determined that no-one will ever receive less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, age, disability, religion, belief, sexual orientation, marital status, race, veteran status or any basis covered by appropriate law.

title: Senior Applied AI Engineer, Document Intelligence
description:
Headquarters: New Jersey, USA

URL: https://vertican.com 

About the role

For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.

We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.

We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.

You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.

This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.

What you will do

Design the pipelines. Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.

We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.

Evaluate new systems before we adopt them. Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.

Build the evaluation process. You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline. 

Ship and operate. Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.

Set direction. Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.

What we are looking for

Required 

- 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.

- Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.

- Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.

- Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.

- You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.

- Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.

- Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.

- Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.

Nice to have 

- Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.

- Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.

- Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.

- Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.

- Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.

How we work and what we offer

Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.

What we offer:

- A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software

- Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.

- Monthly payments in USD

Vertican is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

title: Data Scientist, Trust & Safety
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

You’ll join the Detection subdomain within Trust & Safety, whose mission is to protect the Vinted community by identifying harmful content and activities. We build detection capabilities that enable timely prevention and moderation, reducing members’ exposure to harm, while minimising disruption to legitimate members.

You’ll develop and improve machine learning models that identify harmful listings and suspicious behaviour across the marketplace, while minimising friction on legitimate members. Working with text, images and behavioural data, you’ll apply practical machine learning techniques to evolving detection challenges.

You’ll work closely with Data Scientists, Decision Scientists, Product Managers and engineers to turn ideas into reliable production solutions. You’ll take ownership of well-defined projects across the ML lifecycle, from understanding the data and developing models to deployment, evaluation and ongoing maintenance.

In this position, you’ll 

- Develop, evaluate and improve machine learning models that detect harmful content and behaviour at scale.

- Engineer features, prepare training and evaluation datasets, understanding their limitations and addressing issues such as noisy labels, class imbalance and data leakage.

- Collaborate with engineers to integrate models into production and develop reliable training and inference pipelines using established tooling.

- Work with Decision Scientists and Product Managers to define success metrics and evaluate model improvements through offline analysis and online experimentation, balancing detection coverage with false positives and member experience.

- Monitor deployed models, investigate changes in their effectiveness and improve them as harmful behaviour and underlying data evolve.

- Write reliable, maintainable and reproducible code, document your work, share learnings and contribute ideas to the team’s roadmap.

About you 

- Practical experience developing machine learning solutions, with a solid foundation in machine learning, statistics and probability theory.

- Proficiency in Python and SQL, and experience with ML libraries such as scikit-learn or PyTorch.

- Hands-on experience preparing training datasets, engineering features, training models and evaluating them against baselines and metrics.

- Experience applying machine learning to at least one of the following: tabular or behavioural data, natural language processing, or computer vision.

- Familiarity with the production ML lifecycle, including deployment, monitoring and retraining.

- Ability to break down problems into manageable steps, work independently within an agreed scope and seek input when needed.

- Ability to communicate your approach, findings and trade-offs clearly, collaborate with technical and non-technical colleagues, and learn from feedback.

- Motivation to apply machine learning to member safety, with care for data privacy and the consequences of incorrect predictions.

Nice to have 

- Experience with fraud detection, content classification or other Trust & Safety applications.

- Experience with transformers, multimodal models or LLM-based workflows.

Work perks 

- The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme

- 25 days of paid annual leave

- Newest MacBook models

- Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family

- Frequent team-building events

- Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture

- Lunch benefit per working day

- A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted

- Collective Defined Contribution Pension plan

- NS Business Card for your commute to the office by public transport

- Company bike leasing scheme

- Monthly budget for a flexible benefits platform

- Work from Home allowance 

- A dog-friendly office

Working at Vinted 

Workation policy 

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget 

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Hybrid work 

Our hybrid model, with 2 recommended office days a week, gives you and your team the flexibility to decide if and when you want to work from home, and when to catch up in person.

Equal opportunity 

We welcome applications from everybody, regardless of your background, identity, or life experiences. Job openings come with guides, not checklists. If you’re excited about a role, but don’t identify with every point in the ‘About you’ section, apply anyway – you might still be the perfect match!

€53.900 — €72.900 EUR

title: Cloud Architect
description:
About Vitestro 

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™) . This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement. 

We are looking for a Cloud Architect to shape and implement Vitestro's cloud platform with a clear, pragmatic technical direction. Our infrastructure runs on AWS and supports mission-critical, regulated medical device software. Vitestro is also realizing its first integration with Laboratory Information System (LIS) over the cloud, and delivering that connection is a core part of this role. We need someone who translates real operational and business constraints into working systems — someone whose first instinct is "what does this actually need to do, reliably and affordably," not "what's the most sophisticated way to solve this."

You will join the Platform & Connectivity team and build alongside its cloud, backend, and DevOps engineers. This is an individual-contributor technical leadership role, not a people-management position — you carry the architectural vision and build it hands-on with the team, rather than designing something for others to execute.

If you'd rather ship a solid, working solution than iterate endlessly toward a theoretically ideal one, and you have a track record of keeping cloud costs under control at scale, you'll thrive in this role.

First months at Vitestro 

In your first months, you get to know our cloud platform, the device connectivity and the team. You review the current architecture, its costs and its production-readiness, and identify where the biggest risks and quick wins are. You take ownership of the cloud architecture for our first LIS integration, and you agree with the team on the first architectural standards for observability, logging and infrastructure as code.

This is what success looks like: 

After 12 months, our first LIS integration runs reliably in production, with monitoring, alerting and failure handling in place. Cloud costs are predictable and under control, and key architectural decisions and trade-offs are recorded. The team uses shared patterns instead of reinventing solutions, and is confident running production systems as we move from pre-market to post-market.

Key Responsibilities: 

- Set the technical direction for our AWS-based cloud platform and build it hands-on with the team — weighing cost, operability, and production-readiness as first-class concerns, not afterthoughts

- Own the cloud architecture of Vitestro's first LIS integration over the cloud: secure, reliable, and traceable data exchange between our platform and the hospital laboratory

- Choose solutions on their merits rather than defaulting to the most AWS-native option — including other clouds, self-hosted tooling, or dedicated infrastructure when that's genuinely the better fit

- Take implementations from a working prototype to something that's production-ready — monitoring, alerting, and failure handling included. You bring experience with production systems and advise the team on how to navigate from pre-market to post-market stages.

- Establish architectural standards and patterns so similar problems (e.g. observability, logging, data pipelines) get solved consistently instead of reinvented each time

- Keep cloud costs in check as part of everyday engineering decisions, catching expensive mistakes before they show up on an invoice

- Balance short-term solutions driven by business needs and deadlines against the long-term architecture: make each trade-off explicit, record it, and plan the path from the tactical fix to the durable solution

- Diagnose and resolve production issues across the cloud platform from logs, metrics, and traces

What You’ll Bring: 

- Deep, hands-on production experience with AWS at scale — not certification-level familiarity, but real experience with what breaks and what gets expensive as usage grows

- Proven experience running production systems end to end, from design and release through monitoring and incident response, and the ability to advise a team that is new to production

- Genuine experience building outside an AWS-only mindset — another cloud, self-hosted/open-source alternatives, or dedicated/on-premise infrastructure — enough to make an informed trade-off, not just AWS as the only tool you reach for

- A track record of finishing what others started: turning a partial or unstable implementation into something genuinely reliable in production

- Strong Infrastructure as Code practice (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, or AWS CDK) as the authoritative source of environment configuration

- Comfortable operating in a regulated, security-conscious environment where architecture decisions have compliance implications

- Familiarity with AWS cost structure, along with the ability to factor in cost-related considerations when designing infrastructure

- Professional English; Dutch is a plus

Nice to have: 

- Experience specifically with observability/logging platforms at scale (e.g. OpenSearch, Grafana/Loki stacks, or equivalent) — bringing an implementation to production-hardened state, not just standing it up

- Experience in medical device, healthcare, or another regulated industry

- Familiarity with multi-tenant, per-customer cloud architectures (e.g. isolated accounts or workloads per client/region)

- Experience in a startup or scale-up environment

How We Work 

At Vitestro, ownership is not a slogan - it is an expectation. We trust people to take responsibility, make decisions, and drive work forward.

We believe breakthroughs happen when talented people combine dedication, accountability, and teamwork. That means:

- We take initiative rather than wait for direction.

- We focus on execution and delivering results.

- We proactively remove blockers and help each other succeed.

- We challenge ideas, not people.

- We continuously learn, improve, and raise the bar.

- We celebrate team success over individual heroics.

We move fast, but we do so thoughtfully. We care deeply about quality because the technology we build ultimately impacts patients and healthcare professionals.

If you are looking for an environment where you can make a significant contribution, take ownership of meaningful work, and be surrounded by highly motivated colleagues, we'd love to meet you.

What we offer 

- Competitive salary including a pension plan

- 25 days of annual leave (full-time position)

- A high-skilled team based in Utrecht

- Frequent out-of-work team activities and an annual company weekend away

- A training budget

- The chance to help shape the new niche of autonomous medical robotics

We’re big fans of working from the office – this is where team spirit comes alive. At the same time, we offer flexibility, allowing up to two (out of 5) days of working from home for those who prefer it. 

Are you excited? 

We totally understand that and so are we! By joining us, you can play an active role in changing the future of health care. Excited to join our revolution? Then we’d love to hear from you! 

If you think you've got what it takes, but you don't meet all the requirements - we still recommend you apply. We would love to learn about your interest and experience and consider if you can be a good fit for Vitestro. Nobody is a perfect fit, and we welcome applications with imperfections. We offer a learning environment where we grow together!

Every team has AI. Few have mastered it. Humans were built to adapt, but AI is now moving faster than most workforces can.

Multiverse is the AI adoption layer: the missing link between the AI tools that companies have invested in and the people expected to use them.

Apprenticeships got us started: we’ve trained over a third of the UK’s data and AI apprentices, worked with a third of the FTSE 100, and generated £2bn+ in verified ROI. We closed our latest fundraising round in April 2026, with $500m+ raised in total from VC partners including Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Schroders Capital and Lightspeed. With a $2.1bn valuation, we are Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn, and we are just getting started.

If you want to shape how the workforce wins in the AI era, come and join us.

The AI Transformation team

AI Transformation is a small, focused squad that is driving Multiverse’s next wave of growth. Our mandate is to rebuild how the company actually works, function by function, and to establish the practices that make Multiverse an AI-first company from the core out.

But our work doesn’t stop there. We are building a product that we will take to market to truly be a transformation partner to our customers. Joining this team means shaping the future of Multiverse, of our customers, and of the wider workforce as we navigate the new world of work.

The team is high velocity, inherently cross-functional and broad in scope. We work alongside colleagues whose work we are reimagining, and closely with the wider engineering org building Multiverse's current customer-facing product. The structure is flat and fast, with egos left at the door, bias to action and fun at our core.

What your day-to-day will look like

Every day will be different, but you can expect it to include:

Own and deliver end-to-end AI systems: agents and the platforms they depend on. You identify a user problem, break it down and build the AI system that solves it, in close partnership with the teams who will adopt it

Build evaluation frameworks. You build automated eval pipelines and human-in-the-loop review processes that tell the team whether its AI systems are doing what they should.

Design tool integrations. Agents are only as capable as the systems and context they can reach. You design and build the tool layer: MCPs, APIs, data contracts, and the error handling that makes tool use reliable.

Influence technical direction. You have opinions about how things should be built, and you back them up with evidence. You contribute to architectural decisions, push back when the team is heading in the wrong direction, and propose better approaches.

- Production AI Agent Engineering: You have shipped AI systems that serve real users at scale. - Product mindset: Your natural instinct is to identify the real user pain, understand their requirements and build pragmatic, high-impact solutions. You test, learn and iterate fast, and are comfortable executing under high ambiguity

- Full-Stack Delivery: You work across the stack: LLM integration, backend services, data pipelines, and enough frontend to ship end to end

- Health and wellbeing: Bupa private medical insurance, a medical cash back plan, therapy through Spill and gym access through Wellhub.

- Equity for all : we believe that when Multiverse wins, we all win, which is why every permanent employee receives share options.

- Financial security: life insurance at 3x salary, a workplace pension with 4% contribution from us, Cycle to Work and a Tech Scheme.

- Family support: enhanced maternity and paternity leave, adoption and shared parental leave, paid leave after pregnancy loss, and a workplace nursery scheme.

title: Senior Applied Scientist, Efficient LLM Inference & Model Optimization
description:
About Nebius: 

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

Nebius Token Factory is looking for scientists who can turn frontier LLM and VLM inference bottlenecks into research questions, conduct rigorous experiments, and translate their findings into production capabilities. You will own focused research and optimization projects, write strong code, and produce prototypes, publications, and technical artifacts that engineers can build on.

Your research will span quantization, distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, and model/runtime co-optimization, alongside inference engines and distributed inference architectures. You will investigate how these approaches interact, evaluate their trade-offs across model quality, latency, throughput, memory footprint, and cost per token, and work with engineering teams to bring promising results into production.

Your responsibilities

- Lead research projects in efficient LLM and VLM inference, from hypotheses and experiments through ablations, prototypes, and production handoff.

- Develop and evaluate methods spanning quantization, quantization-aware training (QAT), distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, KV-cache compression, long-context inference, MoE routing, and model/runtime co-optimization.

- Build prototypes using PyTorch, Triton, CUDA-adjacent tooling, or inference-serving frameworks, and collaborate with MLEs and platform engineers to turn them into production components.

- Research LLM request routing and scheduling strategies, including cache-aware load balancing and prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD). Evaluate how queueing, KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and prefill/decode capacity allocation affect latency, throughput, and serving cost.

- Investigate multi-node inference for dense and mixture-of-experts models, including wide expert parallelism (WideEP). Study expert placement, load imbalance, and computation/communication trade-offs, and use the findings to guide model and system architecture choices.

- Develop rigorous evaluations covering quality, latency, throughput, numerical stability, memory footprint, tail latency, and cost per token. Compare serving architectures under consistent workload conditions and GPU budgets.

- Work with MLE, GPU kernel, backend infrastructure, product, and customer teams to select research priorities with measurable production impact.

- Share results through internal reports, technical blogs, papers, and open-source artifacts, and mentor engineers and scientists on experimental design, scientific rigor, and model/system trade-offs.

Must-haves

- A PhD in computer science, machine learning, ML systems, computer systems, computer architecture, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, or a closely related discipline.

- A strong publication record or equivalent research artifacts in ML, ML systems, efficient inference, model compression, quantization, distillation, serving systems, or related areas.

- Strong Python and PyTorch implementation skills, with the ability to turn ideas into experiments and working prototypes.

- Deep knowledge of LLMs, VLMs, transformer inference, decoding algorithms, model compression, quantization, and production-serving trade-offs.

- Strong experimental design skills covering ablations, baselines, metrics, statistical reasoning, and failure analysis.

- Excellent written and verbal communication.

Nice-to-haves

- First-author publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys, ACL, EMNLP, ASPLOS, OSDI, SOSP, ISCA, or HPCA.

- Experience deploying ML models or inference optimizations in production.

- Experience with vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA Dynamo, FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, CUDA, or PyTorch internals.

- Experience applying post-training, SFT, DPO, RLHF, RLAIF, preference optimization, or synthetic data generation to inference quality or efficiency.

- Open-source research artifacts, widely used benchmarks, technical blogs, or invited talks demonstrating contributions to efficient AI systems.

- Research or implementation experience in one or more areas of distributed inference system architecture, such as LLM request routing, PDD, multi-node serving, or MoE expert parallelism, including WideEP.

title: Senior Product Designer (UX/UI)
description:
Optics11 is a fast-growing high-tech company based in Amsterdam, developing advanced fiber optic sensing systems for the most demanding environments. Our technology detects the earliest signs of failure in critical assets – from high-voltage energy infrastructure to subsea and defense applications – and gives our customers precise, real-time data they can act on.

The Role 

As Senior Product Designer you shape how our customers and operators experience Optics11’s end-to-end underwater security solutions: from in-field sensor data acquisition, through data processing, to the software platform where that data is exposed and acted on. You combine user research with hands-on UX/UI design: you understand users in the field, turn those insights into workflows and interface designs, and hand over clear, build-ready designs to our front-end developers. You are part of the Product team in Underwater Security and work closely with Product Management, R&D, Engineering, Data Science, Software, Sales, Projects and Application Engineering.

No two weeks will look the same. You might join an Application Engineer in the field, interview operators and technicians, trace how sensor data flows from the field to the operator’s screen, prototype a new workflow in Figma, or review a front-end implementation with the developers. You own the user experience of our software platform, from research insight to interface design, and make sure real user needs guide decisions across technical, product and commercial teams.

Within your first 6–12 months, you will establish a shared, evidence-based view of our users through personas, journey maps and a structured insight repository; evolve our design system and UI guidelines for the software platform; and deliver interface designs for priority platform features that our developers can build with confidence. This reduces development risk and helps us deliver technology customers can trust in demanding, high-stakes environments

Responsibilities 

- Lead user and customer research: plan and run qualitative, quantitative and field studies across installation, operation and maintenance (for example alongside our Application Engineers), and translate findings into product and design decisions.

- Design the user experience of our software platform: turn product requirements from Product Management and the Product Owner into information architecture, user flows and interaction patterns for complex, data-rich operator workflows (detect, assess, identify and classify), from early concepts to interactive prototypes.

- Propose and hand over UI designs to front-end developers: create high-fidelity, build-ready designs and specifications, align on feasibility with developers and the Product Owner, and review implementations for quality and consistency.

- Own end-to-end customer journeys: map the experience from in-field deployment and data acquisition through data processing to the software platform, including demo flows and supporting internal processes.

- Manage personas and customer insights: maintain the persona set and a central research repository, and synthesise learnings collected across the organisation.

- Validate and measure outcomes: run usability tests before and after release, define adoption and usability metrics, and report impact to stakeholders.

- Evolve and maintain our design system: extend the existing basis with UI components, patterns and guidelines that keep the platform consistent, accessible and efficient to develop.

- Partner across the organisation: work closely with Product Management, Product Ownership and System Architecture, as well as Sales, Business Development, Application Engineering, Support and Marketing, to prioritise development, reduce product risk and advance user-centred practices.

Requirements 

- Master’s degree in interaction design, human-computer interaction, computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

- 5+ years of experience in UX or product design, covering both user research and hands-on UX/UI design, preferably in defense or other technical, high-stakes industries.

- A portfolio showing end-to-end work, from research and workflows to high-fidelity UX/UI for data-rich professional software (e.g. situational-awareness, control-room or analytics applications).

- Experience working on integrated software platforms rather than isolated websites or prototypes.

- Experience handing designs over to front-end developers and working with and evolving a design system, with a working understanding of front-end technology and its constraints.

- Proficiency in qualitative and quantitative research methods, with the ability to translate data into actionable insights and design proposals.

- Understanding of end-to-end systems in which sensor data is acquired in the field, processed and exposed on a software platform, ideally in complex or regulated environments.

- Able to translate complex technical workflows and data into clear, intuitive interfaces, with strong attention to visual detail, consistency and quality.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; able to present research and designs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Proficiency in Figma and in research and collaboration tools such as Jira Product Discovery, Dovetail and Miro.

- Willingness to travel and do field research.

- Driver’s license B (or international equivalent).

- Ability to pass a background / security screening by the Dutch AIVD/MIVD, as you will be working with clients in the defense industry.

Nice to Have 

- Big plus: Experience with underwater acoustics or sonar software.

- Plus: Experience in design leadership, or in setting up design practices in a growing organisation.

- Plus: Front-end skills (e.g. HTML/CSS, React) for prototyping next to AI based tooling.

- Plus: Proficiency in Dutch.

Screening 

You will work with clients in the defense and security sectors. Obtaining a Certificate of No Objection issued by the AIVD, the Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service, is mandatory. This means you will need to undergo a security screening. We will explain the process and guide you through the applicable requirements.

title: Product Engineer, Nino

CoinTracker is on a mission to unlock everyone's financial potential so they can build the life they want. More on Nino: Comprehensive tax and financial planning strategies are currently locked behind high AUM fees or require enough wealth to have a family office. We are turning expert judgment into software so we can serve millions. AI is going to redefine how people understand their finances and how tax advice gets delivered. Not in ten years, in 2026. Nino sits inside CoinTracker ($100M raised, partnered with Coinbase, TurboTax, H&R Block, and Thomson Reuters) with the autonomy of an early-stage startup and the reach of an established platform.

- 
Customers rely on what you build. You've shipped meaningful features end to end, with evidence that customers use them and find them valuable.

- 
More financial work gets done. Workflows you own help households and advisors complete tasks with less manual effort, fewer handoffs, and clearer next steps.

- 
The experience holds up. Your features are easy to use and reliable in practice, including when information is missing, an integration fails, or a person needs to step in.

- 
We learn and ship faster. You turn ambiguous problems into focused releases, learn from real usage, and use that evidence to decide what to improve next.

What you will do 

- 
Examples of what you could build:

- 
Trading: Help users go from an investment idea to a reviewed trade, with clear approvals, execution status, and visibility into what happened.

- 
Strategies: Build ways to discover financial ideas, understand their upside and tradeoffs, explore how they fit a household's situation, and turn a saved strategy into a plan of action.

Tax filing: Bring document collection, missing-information requests, CPA review, and filing progress into one clear experience for households and their tax team.

Across these features, you'll:

- 
Own problems from discovery to launch. Talk with customers and financial experts, identify what matters, and decide what to build first.

- 
Design the experience. Sketch, prototype, and refine interfaces with our designer. Make complex decisions and workflows feel clear.

- 
Build across the stack. Ship interfaces, backend services, integrations, and AI workflows. Follow the problem wherever the implementation takes you.

- 
Turn agents into useful products. Build ways for people to understand, review, and approve an agent's work, including workflows that span external tools and websites.

-

What we look for

Role-agnostic

Exceptional collaboration: You make the people around you better: engineers, designers, CPAs, and Financial Planners. You seek feedback, say what you think, and follow through.

Strong engineering fundamentals. You've built and shipped working software, can reason through unfamiliar systems, and care about correctness and maintainability.

Product judgment. You can turn an open-ended problem into a useful first release, explain what you left out, and define how you'll know it helped.

- 
Design taste. You notice confusing interactions, care about the details, and can explain how your changes improve the experience.

- 
You ship your own work. You're comfortable moving between the interface and backend, using AI coding tools thoughtfully, and verifying the result.

- 
Bonus: startup, agent, or integration experience. You've built directly with users, worked with browser automation or AI agents, or connected systems that don't fit neatly together.

Prior experience with finance, AI or ML products, or our exact tech stack isn't required. Neither is a particular degree or school. We're interested in what you've built and how you think.

About the role 

We are looking for a SIP Expert to own the telephony layer that connects ElevenAgents voice agents to the phone network. SIP traffic is moving from early adoption to large enterprise call volumes, so the hard problems are now reliability and latency at scale.

Your general responsibilities will include: 

- 
Owning SIP end to end, from design doc to implementation, testing and ongoing operation, for a product used by enterprises at scale.

- 
Making call flows such as warm transfers dependable, and simplifying how our call services communicate with each other.

- 
Diagnosing and fixing load-related failures such as resource exhaustion and dropped connections.

- 
Collaborating with support, infrastructure and other teams to turn customer needs into shipped features.

Specific responsibilities might include: 

- 
Making our SIP edge and routing layer production-ready for large enterprise traffic.

- 
Designing and shipping lightweight, lower-latency call-handling services.

- 
Supporting carrier and SIP trunk integrations for enterprise customers.

You will join a small team of five, reporting directly to the team lead, with a high degree of ownership and very little bureaucracy.

Requirements 

We do not require any formal experience, certifications, or degrees. Instead, we are seeking enthusiastic engineers who can showcase solving impressively hard problems with artifacts such as past projects, designs, or open source contributions.

We do require: 

- 
Experience building and operating large-scale SIP/VoIP systems in production, including debugging load-related failures such as port exhaustion, dropped connections and state shared across services

- 
Hands-on experience running LiveKit (or comparable real-time media infrastructure) at scale, with comfort in WebSockets, WebRTC and RTP

- 
Strong backend engineering in Go or a comparable systems language, and a record of owning projects from design document through launch and maintenance

- 
Based in Europe or a nearby time zone, with at least 2 to 3 hours of daily overlap with CET

Bonus: Hands-on experience with Kamailio (or OpenSIPS/FreeSWITCH), or carrier and SIP trunk interconnects.

Location 

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Europe or nearby time zones, with the ability to operate in GMT to GMT+4 time zones preferred. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Dublin, London and Warsaw.

description:
The Role 

We've grown to roughly 265 people working onsite from our Menlo Park headquarters, supported by a large network of remote U.S.-licensed clinicians â and part of the Series C is earmarked for acquisitions. The systems and the spaces holding all of that together were built for a much smaller company. We're hiring a Director of IT & Workplace to own them properly.

You'll own two halves of the same problem: the employee technology platform â identity, endpoints, networking, the SaaS portfolio, and our IT security posture â and the physical environment the company runs on, from space planning and physical security to the AV that customer demos and all-hands depend on. You'll inherit a small, capable team and be accountable for leveling it up. You'll be the named owner for IT controls in our HIPAA and SOC 2 programs, you'll own the IT and workplace budget, and when we acquire a company, you'll be the one integrating it.

Our Environment 

- Identity and access: Okta for SSO, MFA, and lifecycle provisioning.

- Productivity: Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, both in active use across the company.

- Endpoints: a Mac-primary fleet with Windows machines alongside it, managed through MDM. VDIs included.

- Internal systems: IRU, plus a growing portfolio of internal and third-party SaaS applications.

- Workplace: a Palo Alto headquarters with conference room AV and access control, plus a distributed clinician and staff population.

What You'll Do 

Strategy, budget, and team 

- Own a multi-year IT and workplace roadmap tied to the hiring plan, and bring it to leadership with clear tradeoffs and funding asks.

- Own the IT and workplace operating and capital budget: forecast it, defend it in planning cycles, and continuously rationalize license, vendor, and facilities spend.

- Lead, coach, and grow the existing team â set clear expectations, run honest performance conversations, hire as scope deepens, and build career paths that keep strong people.

- Define and publish service levels for ticket response, uptime, onboarding readiness, and workplace turnaround, and report against them to the executive team.

Technology and infrastructure
