- Own the endpoint fleet and the SaaS portfolio â Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, IRU, and a long tail of business applications â with enforced MDM baselines for encryption, patching, and configuration.

- Own network and connectivity for the headquarters and the remote workforce, with redundancy appropriate to a company our customers depend on.

- Replace manual provisioning, access reviews, and device setup with scripted, auditable workflows.

- Lead major programs end to end: platform migrations, upgrades, office buildouts, and the IT and workplace integration of acquired companies.

Security, compliance, and risk 

- Serve as the accountable owner for IT controls in our HIPAA, SOC 2, and customer security review programs, including evidence collection and audit response.

- Enforce least privilege across the environment and run recurring access certifications with documented outcomes.

- Partner with Security on incident response and vulnerability remediation, and with Legal on data handling, retention, and discovery requests.

- Own business continuity and disaster recovery for corporate systems â write the plans, test them, and fix what the tests expose.

- Treat protected health information and confidential data with the care our customers and their patients expect. This is non-negotiable in everything we do.

Workplace and facilities 

- Own day-to-day operations of the headquarters, and lead space planning and buildouts against a hiring plan that keeps moving.

- Manage physical security â access control and badging, visitor management, cameras, and emergency preparedness â aligned with our compliance obligations.

- Own conference room and event AV, including all-hands and customer visits, to a standard where the technology is never the story.

- Support remote clinicians and staff with reliable equipment logistics, home office standards, and consistent service regardless of location.

- Manage facilities, AV, security, and food vendors, plus landlord and lease matters, in partnership with Finance and Legal.

What You'll Bring 

- 8+ years in IT , spanning hands-on administration or engineering and progressively senior ownership. You've done the work you'll now be leading.

- 3+ years managing IT or workplace teams , including hiring, performance management, and developing people into bigger roles.

- Proven ownership of an IT function through rapid growth. You've scaled systems and process ahead of headcount, not behind it.

- Deep technical expertise across identity (Okta or comparable), Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, MDM at fleet scale, and corporate networking.

- Experience as a named control owner in a regulated environment â HIPAA, SOC 2, or HITRUST â including sitting across the table from auditors.

- Workplace or facilities exposure â buildouts, moves, physical security, or lease management â or a genuine appetite to own it and learn quickly.

Nice to Have

- Automation depth (Python, Bash, PowerShell) and experience managing devices and infrastructure as code.

Reinvent healthcare with AI that puts safety first. Weâre building the worldâs first healthcareâonly, safetyâfocused LLM â a breakthrough platform designed to transform patient outcomes at a global scale. This is category creation.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Verticals (AI Native)
description:
Headquarters: Canada

URL: http://www.life360.com 

About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 107.7 million monthly active users (MAU), as of September 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries. 

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com .

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above. 

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

This role sits on the Verticals team within Life360 — the group building the next frontier of meaningful connection beyond the core family circle. This role's initial focus is Aging in Place: helping aging parents stay safely independent while giving the families around them real peace of mind. Over time, this role may flex to support other emerging verticals — Things (Tile, connected trackers) or Pets — as priorities shift, so we're looking for someone who wants to help define the pattern for new member segments, not just ship one feature set.

We are a product-minded, AI-Native engineering team. That means AI isn't just a tool we use — it's how we work. We've redesigned our team workflows around AI, treating it as a first-class collaborator at every stage: ideation, coding, testing, review, and iteration. We ship faster and go deeper because of it, and we're looking for someone who wants to help define what that looks like at scale.

About the Job

Life360 is hiring an AI Native Senior Software Engineer — a senior engineer who doesn't just use AI tools, but thinks natively in them. You'll be central to how the Verticals team builds products.

You'll design and build features that serve one of our most important and fastest-growing member segments: aging parents who want to stay safely connected with, and independent from, the families who care about them. As priorities change, you may also apply these same patterns to Things (connected trackers) or Pets.

You will take full ownership of what you build from the first line of code through production, on-call, and the member impact it has. You obsess over the humans on the other end of the product, not just the ticket.

Full-stack experience is required for this role — you should be comfortable moving between backend services and the mobile surfaces that expose them. Our stack spans Spring Boot microservices, Java, Kafka, and Kafka Streams on the backend, a modern cloud-native platform on AWS, and native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) apps on the client side.

In your first year, success looks like having shipped end-to-end features serving the Aging in Place member segment and establishing at least one AI-native workflow the broader team adopts.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $103,500 to $192,000 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is 149,500 to 177,500 CAD. Note: Please be aware that the job title for positions in Canada will be "Developer" in lieu of "Engineer." We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers. 

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) , as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits. 

What You’ll Do

- Ship end-to-end across the stack — from backend services and APIs through to the iOS and Android surfaces members use, serving tens of millions of users — moving between layers as the feature demands.

- Work with AI (Claude Code) as a first-class collaborator — orchestrate agents to create specs, generate code, and perform reviews, moving faster without sacrificing quality.

- Define and codify AI-Native engineering practices for the Verticals team, establishing playbooks the broader org can adopt.

- Collaborate closely with product managers and designers to turn complex user problems into scalable engineering solutions.

- Contribute to architectural decisions, code reviews, and a culture of craft and continuous improvement.

- Participate in on-call rotation and incident response.

- Mentor team members and contribute to team processes and technical standards.

- Support performance, reliability, and accessibility across the features you own.

- Adapt patterns and services built for Aging in Place to future verticals (Things, Pets) as team scope expands.

What We’re Looking For

- 4+ years of experience building and operating high-quality, consumer-scale services.

- 1+ years of hands-on experience prompting, evaluating, and building with LLMs.

- Full-stack proficiency spanning backend services (Java, Spring Boot, Kafka) and mobile client development (Swift for iOS and/or Kotlin for Android), with the versatility to work across the whole stack as needed.

- Hands-on experience with agentic workflows, prompt engineering, context window management, and MCP/function calling.

- A track record of using AI tooling to multiply your own output — not just as autocomplete, but as a development partner.

- A strong sense of ownership — you don't wait to be told what to fix, and you follow through past "it works on my machine" to "it works for the member, in production, at scale."

- Strong communication and collaboration skills — you work well with product, design, and platform engineers.

- Excitement for defining what it means to be AI-Native — you're not waiting for the playbook, you want to write it.

- Empathy for the humans behind the product — an aging parent trying to stay independent, or a family member trying to help from afar.

- Bachelor's Degree in a Technical field, or equivalent experience.

Nice-to-Have 

- Experience with IoT, telematics, or embedded/hardware-adjacent systems.

- Familiarity with Kafka, Kinesis, or other high-throughput streaming platforms.

- Background with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, DataDog).

AI-Native Expectations

We use AI coding tools as a professional standard on this team. Here's what that means in practice:

- Daily use: You use AI coding assistants (we support Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot) for real, substantive tasks: analysis, coding, refactoring, testing, navigating codebases, and documentation. Not just research or autocomplete but as a development partner.

- Judgment and ownership: AI-generated code gets the same review you'd give any PR. You are accountable for everything you ship.

- Velocity: We expect senior engineers who use AI well to operate with meaningful leverage — doing more with the same time, taking on problems that would otherwise require a larger team.

- Team leadership: You share what works. You automate prompting strategies that others can build on and help teammates earlier in their AI workflow adoption get up to speed.

- Continuous learning: The tooling is changing fast. You stay current and bring recommendations to the team when something would meaningfully improve how we work.

Our Benefits

- Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.

- 401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.

- Paid parental leave.

- Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being.

- Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns.

- Learning & Development programs.

- Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.

- Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

AI Usage: We use AI to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Life360 hiring teams

Life360 Values

Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference 

- Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust. 

- Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.

- Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families. 

- High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done. 

Our Commitment to Belonging

Life360 is an equal opportunity employer. We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected status. We believe diverse perspectives make us better, and we’re building a workplace that reflects the communities we serve. Don’t meet every qualification? Apply anyway.

title: Research Engineer, Machine Learning
description:
About Boltz 

Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible.

Boltz was founded by former MIT scientists who created Boltz-1, the first fully commercially available open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3-level accuracy in predicting the 3D structure of biomolecular complexes.

We focus on two things:

- Foundation models. Our open models, Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and BoltzGen, are trusted by 100,000+ scientists across biotech and academia, and used in programs at every Top 20 pharma as well as leading agrichemical and industrial research organizations. Our latest proprietary foundation models power our products and the custom models we build with partners.

- Boltz Lab and the Boltz API. Our products run our latest models, design pipelines (BoltzMol for small molecules, BoltzProt for protein design) and agents as reliable, production-grade tools built around real chemistry and biology workflows. Teams start from a target and a hypothesis, then generate, evaluate, and rank candidate molecules in Boltz Lab, run our models from their own code and agents through the Boltz API, or deploy them inside their own environment.

The two feed each other: our open releases earn scientific credibility and community insight, and our products turn our full range of models into real impact for partners including Pfizer, Takeda, GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb and DSM-Firmenich.

You can read more about our mission, research and product vision in our manifesto .

About the role 
As a Research Engineer (ML), you will push the scale and efficiency of model training at Boltz, and work with researchers to decide where systems work will have the most research impact. You will be an active member of one of our ML research teams, bringing deep systems and scaling expertise to its models and experiments.
This role is ideal for an engineer with deep ML systems expertise who wants to work close to the research and help shape its direction.

What you’ll do 

- Identify the systems work with the highest research impact for your team, and own it end to end.

- Scale model training: distributed and parallel training, larger models, and the problems that appear at scale.

- Profile and optimize across the training stack, from data loading to kernels, communication and the cluster.

- Build research tooling for our cluster, working with Infrastructure & Platform.

- Make what you build reusable across teams, and use what you learn to inform model and experiment design.

About you 

Minimum Requirements

- Hands-on experience training large deep learning models on multi-node GPU clusters.

- Knowledge of the ML training stack end to end from the systems perspective, from data loading and model code through the framework, kernels, communication and the cluster, with depth in at least one layer.

- Strong Python and PyTorch, with a high bar for engineering quality.

- Experience working closely with ML researchers on model and training code.

- A track record of identifying and driving high-impact technical work independently.

Preferred Requirements

- Knowledge of parallelization strategies for large models, including techniques popularized by LLM training such as FSDP or ZeRO, tensor parallelism and sequence parallelism.

- Low-level GPU performance work, such as custom kernels (e.g. CUDA or Triton).

- Experience building tools that others use to run work on a shared GPU cluster.

- Exposure to structure prediction or molecular modeling, or experience using Boltz models.

What we offer 

- Work alongside one of the most talent-dense teams in the field.

- Significant ownership and independence, with responsibility for driving projects from concept to deployment.

- Highly competitive salary with meaningful equity in a public benefit company.

- Benefits: 

- 25 days plus bank holidays a year

- Annual team offsite trip

- Private healthcare (BUPA), covering pre-existing conditions

- Pension program

- Paid parental leave

- Wellhub gym membership

- Free lunch every day

- Travel expenses

How we hire 

- Initial screen with a member of the Talent team

- Diagnosis interview: work through a degraded training run with us (no manual coding test)

- Onsite in London or virtual onsite with the team

- Offer + Onboarding

Our commitment 

Boltz is committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds. If you need any adjustments during the hiring process, tell us and we'll make it work.

title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Actuator Control & Locomotion), Intern
description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

As a Software Engineer intern on Robot Autonomy, you'll train locomotion and low-level control policies for our legged security robots and help take them from simulation to real hardware. You'll work close to the actuators, from joint-level behavior through coordinated locomotion, on robots that patrol outdoor sites across varied terrain and challenging weather.

This role is highly practical: you'll design training setups, run experiments in simulation, transfer policies to physical robots, and measure how they hold up. You'll get hands-on experience with the gap between a policy that works in simulation and one that keeps a robot on its feet on wet ground at night.

What You'll Work On

- Train and evaluate reinforcement learning policies for locomotion and low-level control in simulation.

- Apply sim-to-real techniques such as domain randomization, reward design, and policy robustness methods, and test the results on physical robots.

- Make policies robust to varied terrain, challenging weather, and noisy, delayed, or missing sensor data.

- Explore control approaches that transfer across robot embodiments with different actuators and dynamics.

- Build evaluation workflows with clear metrics and repeatable experiments, in simulation and on hardware.

- Apply solid engineering practices: experiment tracking, version control, reproducible training runs.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for a motivated robotics or machine learning student excited to apply academic training in a fast-moving startup. You'll be surrounded by a team that values learning, experimentation, and building things that actually work in the real world.

Your Background

- Currently pursuing a PhD or recently completed a Master's degree in Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, or a closely related field.

- Hands-on experience training reinforcement learning policies for robot control, in simulation or on hardware.

- Experience with robotics simulators such as Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, or Gazebo.

- Solid grounding in robot dynamics and control.

- Good coding skills in Python, with PyTorch (or JAX).

- Comfortable using Docker and Git in your workflows.

Nice to Have

- Experience deploying learned policies on physical robots, ideally legged.

- Experience with low-level actuator, motor, or joint control.

- C++ and ROS 2 experience.

- Publications at top robotics or ML venues (CoRL, RSS, ICRA, NeurIPS).

What We Offer

- Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

- Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

- Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

- Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

- Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

- Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

About the job

Mistral AI is looking for a Domain Expert in crashworthiness simulations to help build AI-accelerated simulation capabilities for industrial engineering.

You will work at the intersection of industrial simulation, physics modeling, machine learning, and engineering workflows. Your role is to bring deep solid-mechanics expertise into the design, training, evaluation, and deployment of AI Physics Models for real engineering use cases.

You will work with research, product, and customer-facing teams to ensure that our models are useful against real engineering standards — not only benchmark metrics.

Relevant application areas may include automotive crashworthiness, aerospace structures, consumer-electronics drop/reliability, manufacturing, durability/fatigue, and other nonlinear structural mechanics problems.

What you will do

- Work with our research team to define, generate, and iteratively improve simulation datasets for training and evaluating crashworthiness foundation models, balancing coverage of relevant physical scenarios, simulation fidelity, and computational cost.

- Design and run high-fidelity simulation campaigns using structural mechanics solvers such as Abaqus, LS-DYNA, Ansys Mechanical, Radioss or equivalent tools.

- Define the relevant variation space for training data: geometry, mesh resolution, material behavior, boundary conditions, loading, contact, joints, failure modes, and engineering KPIs.

- Build or guide automated pipelines for simulation setup, execution, post-processing, dataset creation, and model evaluation.

- Work with research teams to train and evaluate AI models on simulation data, and diagnose failure modes caused by data gaps, poor coverage, numerical artifacts, or model limitations.

Join Multiverse and power our mission to equip the workforce to win in the AI era.

The Agentic Work Environment team 

The Agentic Work Environment (AWE) owns the environment everyone at Multiverse works in, wherever they are in the world. That covers the devices, workplace tools and accounts colleagues use every day, the platform our product is built and run on, and the identity and access that decide who, or which agent, can do what across all of it. Product teams own what they build; we own the ground it stands on, the path it takes to production, and the baseline standards it meets on the way. Our mission is to make the safe way the fast way for every colleague and the agents they put to work.

For a security-minded AI engineer, that remit runs in two directions. In the product platform, you build security into the path itself: review agents that check every change against our baseline standards, one identity for customers, staff and agents, and detection and response through our SIEM and SOAR, so nobody, person or agent, has to remember to be secure. In the workplace, you secure the devices, tools and accounts colleagues around the world rely on. As more of them put agents to work, whatever their job title, you make sure every agent has its own identity, a named owner, scoped access and evals, so autonomy is earned on evidence rather than granted on trust.

What your day-to-day will look like 

Every day will be different, but you can expect it to include: 

Build security into the path to production. You turn our baseline standards into checks that run on every change: policy as code, review agents that check each change against the baseline and a team's own standards, and gates matched to the risk of what's changing. Staying on the path should meet the security requirements without any extra work.

Secure the agents we and our colleagues build. You threat-model agent systems end to end, from prompt injection and tool misuse to data leaking through context and retrieval, and design the controls that stop it: scoped tool permissions, permission-aware retrieval, sandboxing, and human approval where the risk calls for it.

Give every agent an identity. You build the identity and access layer for agents. Each one has its own identity, a named owner, least-privilege access that is reviewed and can be revoked at once, and a full record of what it did.

Build detection and response with agents. You write detections and automated responses on our SIEM and SOAR, and build agents that triage alerts, gather context and carry out bounded, reversible responses, so people spend their time on the cases that need judgement.

Secure the workplace, worldwide. You apply the same approach to the devices, workplace tools and accounts colleagues use every day: automated controls rather than manual checklists, and access that is granted and removed as people join, move and leave.

Prove it holds with security evals. You build eval pipelines and red-team exercises that show whether our agents and controls stand up to attack, and produce compliance evidence as a by-product of the work rather than as screenshots for an auditor.

Influence technical direction. You have opinions about how things should be built, and you back them up with evidence. You contribute to architectural decisions, push back when the team is heading in the wrong direction, and propose better approaches.

What We Are Looking For 

- Security Engineering: You have built security into systems rather than reviewed it after the fact, across some mix of application and cloud security, identity and access, and detection and response. You understand how AI systems get attacked, through prompt injection, tool misuse and data leaking through context, and you design controls that make the secure option the easy one for the people using them

- Production AI Agent Engineering: You have shipped AI systems that serve real users at scale. You understand the engineering challenges that make agent systems different from conventional software, including context management, model selection and routing, cost engineering, tool use and agent augmentation, and evaluation

- Product mindset: Your natural instinct is to identify the real user pain, understand their requirements and build pragmatic, high-impact solutions. You test, learn and iterate fast, and are comfortable executing under high ambiguity

- Full-Stack Delivery: You work across the stack: LLM integration, backend services, data pipelines, and enough frontend to ship end to end

- Fluent in AI-assisted development and can mentor others to do it well

Benefits

- Health and wellbeing: Bupa private medical insurance, a medical cash back plan, therapy through Spill and gym access through Wellhub.

- Equity for all : we believe that when Multiverse wins, we all win, which is why every permanent employee receives share options.

- Financial security: life insurance at 3x salary, a workplace pension with 4% contribution from us, Cycle to Work and a Tech Scheme.

- Family support: enhanced maternity and paternity leave, adoption and shared parental leave, paid leave after pregnancy loss, and a workplace nursery scheme.

- Hybrid working: 3 days a week in the office - except for Coaches & Instructors who come into the office 1 day per month. Plus 10 days a year to work from anywhere.

- Work perks: quarterly team socials, company-wide events, happy hours, lunch delivered to the office once a week, fully stocked snack bar and a drinks fridge!

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 

We’re an equal opportunities employer. And proud of it. Every applicant and employee is afforded the same opportunities regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. This will never change. Read our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion policy here .

Our Commitment to Safeguarding 

Multiverse is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our learners. We expect all employees to share this commitment and adhere to our Safeguarding Policy , our Prevent Policy and all other Multiverse company policies. About Proxima 

Proxima (formerly VantAI) is advancing an AI-native approach to drug discovery by making protein interactions programmable. Our platform brings together foundation-model machine learning, a scalable data generation engine, and a partnership track record exceeding $5B in collaborations across the world’s leading biopharma and tech organizations. We’ve recently closed an oversubscribed seed round partnering us with an elite group of sophisticated and dedicated VCs including DCVC, Nvidia’s Nventures, AIX, Yosemite among others.

Neo-1 is our all-atom foundation model that combines state-of-the-art structure prediction and molecular generation in a single system. Neo-1 enables rapid exploration of chemical and structural space for high value, previously intractable targets, and in particular unlocks small molecule proximity therapeutics like molecular glues with AI for the first time.

In parallel, we are developing an advanced structural interactomics platform built on proprietary XLMS technology and a lab equipped with next-generation mass spectrometry instrumentation. This platform produces proteome-scale maps of protein interactions and helps identify small molecules that modulate proximity. Together with Neo-1, it creates an integrated system capable of co-folding protein complexes while generating candidate small molecules to influence those interactions.

Proximity-based therapeutics represent one of most promising frontiers in modern drug discovery with the potential to treat previously intractable diseases and target ‘undruggable’ proteins. Our technology combines proteome-scale structural data with state-of-the-art generative AI foundation models, and coupled with our talented team of scientists and engineers we are uniquely well-positioned to discover and develop a new class of medicines. Come join us!

About You: 

Proxima is seeking highly-motivated Computational Biologists interested in building the leading AI-enabled drug discovery platform for novel induced proximity therapeutic modality.

Successful candidates will work closely with the Computational Chemistry, Machine Learning and Application Engineering teams to tap into the wealth of evolutionary, structural and -omics data to unlock the full potential of unified machine learning representations and large-scale geometric deep learning generative models.

Projects may include designing large-scale scientific workflows for mining public and unique in-house data; developing novel systems biology and structural biology computational methods, tools and algorithms; and/or designing, training and fine-tuning best-in-class machine learning models. In our projects we apply induced proximity approaches to some of the most challenging targets considered “undruggable” as well as discover, build and develop novel proximity platforms spanning across multiple targets and disease areas.

We value individuals who want to make an impact, have a deep intellectual curiosity, enjoy solving challenging problems and have a track record of achievement. At Proxima, we believe that success is determined by talent and hard work, and individuals are given equal opportunities to grow and advance based on their abilities and contributions.

Key Responsibilities:

Preferred Qualifications:

Server Infrastructure is a Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) team responsible for the full lifecycle of Nebius Cloud hardware: from newly delivered bare metal through provisioning, operation, maintenance, and decommissioning. Almost every Nebius service runs on servers within our domain. Our mission is to make the hardware layer fast, reliable, and invisible.

We apply software engineering to infrastructure operations. We build services and automation that bring servers into the cloud, keep them healthy, recover them from failures, and retire them safely. Our work spans CPU and GPU platforms, the base GNU/Linux system, and the infrastructure supporting our hardware fleet.

- Define meaningful reliability indicators and service level objectives, using them to guide engineering priorities.

- Reduce operational toil by turning recurring failures and manual procedures into reliable automation.

- Improve on-call practices, incident response, and learning through blameless incident reviews.

title: Research Engineer Privacy and Anonymization
description:
Location: San Francisco or Singapore (on-site), or remote (Singapore or US Pacific time zones)
Start Date: ASAP
Languages: English
Team: Engineering

About the Role

Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. Their marketplace helps the people who create data get value for it, and gives AI labs trustworthy data to train on. It is already used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs, and the company is backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand.

We are looking for a Research Engineer, Privacy and Anonymization to build the systems that make sensitive, real-world data safe and still useful for AI training. You will develop methods to detect and remove personally identifiable information, secrets and other sensitive content from raw data before it enters processing and synthetic data pipelines â protecting privacy without destroying the structure and signal that make the data valuable for training agents.

This is a privacy and data-protection engineering seat, not a synthetic-task design role. You will own the pipeline that stands in front of downstream processing, training, evaluation and synthetic generation.

This is a full-time role, starting ASAP. Offices are in San Francisco and Singapore; remote candidates are welcome if their working hours can overlap about 70â80% with either San Francisco (US Pacific) or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring.

What You'll Do

- Build systems to detect PII, quasi-identifiers, credentials and other sensitive information, and design transformations based on the data type and the downstream use case.

- Develop and benchmark detection approaches that combine rules, statistical models, classifiers and LLM-based methods.

- Build production pipelines that anonymize raw data before it enters downstream processing, training, evaluation or synthetic data generation.

- Create evaluation frameworks that measure privacy risk and retained data utility, including recall-weighted metrics, leakage tests and adversarial re-identification attempts.

- Design systems that stay robust to new data sources, schema drift, unusual formats and sensitive information embedded in unexpected fields.

- Work with engineering, research, operations and customers to translate privacy requirements into practical technical policies and safeguards.

What We're Looking For

- Strong proficiency in Python, and experience building reliable production data or machine-learning systems.

- Experience with information extraction, named-entity recognition, classification, or related methods for detecting rare or sensitive content.

- Strong experimental instincts, and the ability to compare approaches across recall, precision, latency, cost and downstream data utility.

- An understanding of the difference between redaction, masking, pseudonymization, anonymization and synthetic data â and when each is appropriate.

- High attention to detail, and the ability to reason about subtle leakage paths, edge cases and adversarial failure modes.

- Experience building data-processing pipelines end to end, including where there was no fully prescribed roadmap.

- Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating across teams and time zones.

- Strong candidates may also have hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (such as differential privacy, k-anonymity, secure aggregation or format-preserving encryption); have worked with sensitive data in healthcare, finance or security; have built low-latency or high-throughput ML inference or data-processing systems; or have taken work from early research through to production.

- Technical aptitude and learning potential matter more than years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet every point above.

Why This Role Matters for You

- Make real-world data safe to train on: You will build the systems that let sensitive data be used for AI training without exposing people or secrets.

- Privacy without wrecking utility: The job is not only to redact, but to keep the structure and signal that downstream training and synthetic pipelines need.

- From detection to production: You will own the full path: detection methods, transformations, evaluation, and the pipeline that sits in front of training and generation.

- Hard, high-stakes edge cases: Work on leakage paths, schema drift and adversarial failure modes, not only clean benchmark datasets.

- San Francisco, Singapore, or remote: Work on-site in San Francisco or Singapore, or remotely, with hours that overlap about 70â80% with either US Pacific or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring.

title: Senior Systems Engineer
description:
Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. 
Its offerings include a very energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. 
Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. 
Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges. 
Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions 

Description of the Team/Project 

We are looking for a senior Systems Engineer to join our Program & Systems Engineering department and contribute to the development of our photonic quantum computing systems, including strategic programs such as QBI Phase B and PROQCIMA+.

As our first dedicated Systems Engineer, you will play a key role in ensuring the technical consistency of our complex systems, bringing together photonics, electronics, mechanics, cryogenics and software. You will own the system technical baseline, working with domain experts who contribute to subsystem expertise and detailed technical inputs.

Working closely with multidisciplinary R&D teams and reporting to the CTO, you will operate as a peer of the Program Manager, with a dotted-line relationship for program priorities. You will own the definition and implementation of systems engineering practices, from requirements definition and system architecture to integration, verification and validation. You will provide technical recommendations and escalate unresolved trade-offs to the CTO, while Program and Project Managers own priorities, budgets and delivery planning.

Your Key Responsibilities: 

- System architecture & requirements: Define and maintain system-level requirements, translate them into subsystem specifications, and ensure consistency and traceability throughout development. Own the system architecture and controlled technical baseline, consolidating contributions from domain experts and requirements from customer projects in coordination with the relevant Project Manager. 
- Interface management: Coordinate technical interfaces between subsystems, identify dependencies, and ensure compatibility across engineering disciplines. Establish Interface Control Documents (ICDs), with a named technical owner on each side of each interface. 
- Verification & validation: Define system-level V&V strategies, acceptance criteria to ensure system performance and compliance with requirements. Own the V&V plan and organize requirements and architecture, design, and integration-readiness reviews, with clear readiness criteria and traceability between requirements and verification evidence. 
- Technical coordination & risk management: Assess design trade-offs and support engineering teams in resolving complex integration challenges. Take ownership of technical risks in the shared risk register and propose mitigation actions. Work with Program and Project Managers to assess cost and schedule implications, escalating unresolved disagreements to the CTO. 
- Change control: Assess the technical impact of proposed changes to requirements, architecture, interfaces and supplier specifications or parts. Support the change-control process chaired by the Program Manager, with cost and schedule assessments provided by the Project Manager, and maintain the approved technical baseline. 
- Roadmap contributions: Provide technical inputs to the integrated multi-year roadmap, including technical dependencies, constraints affecting the critical path and readiness criteria for technical gates. Support Program and Project Managers in aligning technical milestones with resources and budgets. 
- Systems engineering processes: Establish and continuously improve pragmatic engineering methodologies, documentation and tools adapted to a fast-growing R&D environment. Define roles, responsibilities and processes before selecting tools. Prioritize requirements and traceability, interface control, change control, technical reviews and V&V; pilot lightweight processes on one project, obtain CTO approval and support wider adoption. 
- Engineering tools: Own requirements and traceability tools, define needs and lead evaluations and pilots for CTO approval. Build on the existing environment and introduce dedicated requirements management or model-based systems engineering (MBSE) tools only when justified by system complexity or practical limitations.

Requirements 

- Engineering degree or equivalent qualification in systems engineering, physics, electronics, photonics, mechatronics or related fields. 
- Solid experience (+8 years) in systems engineering, system architecture, or multidisciplinary system integration, ideally involving complex hardware and software systems. Experience taking technical responsibility for large, complex systems and establishing a controlled requirements and architecture baseline is particularly relevant. 
- Strong understanding of requirements engineering, interface management, technical risk assessment and verification & validation methodologies, including requirements traceability, ICDs and technical change-impact assessment. 
- Ability to integrate domain experts’ contributions into a coherent system architecture and work effectively alongside Program and Project Managers. 
- Ability to structure systems engineering practices while remaining pragmatic and hands-on in an evolving R&D environment. 
- Experience introducing systems engineering processes or tools in a growing organization. Ability to define process needs first and scale tools accordingly; familiarity with requirements management and MBSE approaches is an advantage. 
- Excellent analytical, problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to challenge technical decisions. Ability to explain technical trade-offs, make clear recommendations, and escalate unresolved issues constructively. 
- Professional proficiency in English. 
Benefits 

- Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience 
- Company savings plan
- 100% health coverage (Alan)
- 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
- Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
- Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)

What we offer:

- A team eager to collaborate and grow with you
- A hybrid work model (3-4 days/week onsite in Massy, 1 day in Paris or 1 to 2 days remotely)
- Daily exposure to the entire quantum stack — from high-level APIs to low-level firmware, and everything in between.

Your primary focus will be to work directly with our technical teams and personally draft patent applications and claims , while shaping and implementing an ambitious IP strategy to support Quandela’s growth as a leading photonic quantum computing company.

You will translate complex inventions into effective patent protection across areas such as photonics, semiconductor technologies, quantum hardware, system architectures and computer-implemented inventions. You will not be expected to be an expert in every field: we are looking for someone who can quickly understand unfamiliar technical subjects, ask the right questions and develop robust applications based on input from our researchers and engineers.

You will also serve as a trusted IP counterpart for management, investors and partners, drawing on external patent attorneys and specialist legal counsel across jurisdictions, particularly as Quandela expands its presence in the United States.

** Your key responsibilities

Work directly with inventors and personally draft patent applications 

- Spend a substantial proportion of your time working with technical teams and personally drafting patent applications and claims. 
- Identify inventions through regular interaction with researchers and engineers, and assess their technical contribution and potential scope of protection.
- Lead invention disclosure discussions, clarify complex scientific concepts and identify protection opportunities beyond the initial disclosure.
- Draft clear specifications and robust claims, anticipating prosecution challenges and potential commercial applications.
- Handle prosecution directly where appropriate, and coordinate with external patent attorneys according to jurisdiction, technical needs and workload.
- Ensure that external support complements your own drafting work and meets the required technical and quality standards.
Shape IP strategy and independently drive its implementation

- Advise the C-level on the balance between patents, trade secrets and publications, and on filing priorities, geographical coverage and portfolio maintenance.
- Translate agreed strategic priorities into an actionable IP roadmap, with clear objectives, timelines, budget requirements and measurable outcomes. 
- Take ownership of day-to-day implementation, escalating major strategic, financial or legal decisions to the appropriate C-level stakeholders.
- Conduct targeted patent landscape and competitor analyses to inform portfolio development and business decisions.
- Anticipate future protection needs, including those associated with expansion in the United States and other priority markets.
Coordinate international protection and specialist expertise 

- Coordinate international filings and prosecution across Europe, the United States and Asia, engaging local patent experts as needed.
- Select and manage external advisers based on relevant expertise, quality, responsiveness and cost.
- Draw on and develop a professional network of trusted patent and legal specialists across key jurisdictions.
- Scope and coordinate freedom-to-operate assessments with external specialists, translating findings into practical recommendations.
- Coordinate opposition proceedings and other contentious patent matters with specialist counsel when required.
- Work with legal counsel on IP provisions in research collaborations, joint development agreements and licensing arrangements, including ownership and access rights.
Act as a trusted IP counterpart for management, investors and partners 

- Provide clear, well-supported advice on IP risks, protection opportunities and portfolio priorities.
- Present Quandela’s IP approach and portfolio coherently and credibly in investor discussions and due diligence processes, in coordination with management.
- Support partnerships and potential corporate transactions by coordinating IP analysis and specialist input.
- Explain complex patent matters in terms that enable informed technical and business decisions.
Build practical processes that support delivery

- Manage the IP budget, external counsel relationships and portfolio tools within agreed parameters.
- Build IP awareness through practical guidance and regular interaction with technical teams.

Requirements

- Specialist training in European patent law, such as the CEIPI patent programme or an equivalent European patent training pathway.
- European Patent Attorney qualification strongly preferred. Candidates at an advanced stage towards qualification will also be considered if they demonstrate substantial relevant experience and the seniority to take ownership of the role.
- At least 8 years of professional experience in patent drafting and prosecution , in addition to doctoral research, with a demonstrable record of personally drafting technically complex applications and claims.
- Experience gained in a patent attorney firm, an in-house IP team, or both, with meaningful responsibility for portfolio development and client or business advice.
- Strong technical reasoning and the ability to understand unfamiliar subjects through focused discussions with domain experts. Experience in one or more relevant fields—such as photonics, semiconductors, quantum technologies, electronics or computer-implemented inventions—is expected; expertise across all these fields is not required.

You measure, reconstruct and analyze real samples to find out how well our tool performs, and what holds it back. You work between the optics lab, the algorithm team, and our customers' samples, and you become our in-house expert on system performance.

title: Network Engineer – Ground Station Networking & Integration
description:
About Alta Ares

Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 160 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

The challenge 

Our operators rely on a ground network that carries telemetry, video and control between drones, antennas and stations, often set up in minutes on unfamiliar terrain. Networking is what turns separate radios, computers and antennas into one system that behaves the same way on every unit. You will configure and debug on the bench, automate deployments, and troubleshoot live links during field trials.

Missions 

- Design the ground network: addressing, routing, switching and power over Ethernet between stations and antenna systems.

- Integrate telemetry and video flows: MAVLink routing, video streams, latency and reliability measurements.

- Connect the antenna positioning system to the station: control interface, automatic and manual modes.

- Automate provisioning: reference images, router configurations, scripts and checklists so every unit is identical.

- Secure and track deployed systems: workstation hardening, inventory and versions per serial number.

Required skills 

- Degree in networking, computer or embedded engineering, with experience in network deployment or embedded systems.

- Strong IP networking fundamentals: addressing, VLANs, UDP and multicast, latency and packet-loss diagnostics.

- Tools: Wireshark, router and switch configuration, Windows and Linux, scripting (Python, PowerShell, Bash), Git, Router OS.

- Clear documentation and cybersecurity basics for sensitive environments.

- Autonomous and field-oriented, available for frequent travel.

title: hbo-stage Analyseren kwaliteit bouwvergunningen BAG
description:
hbo- afstudeerstage, vanaf februari 2027 

Ben jij die nieuwsgierige en enthousiaste student die graag in data duikt en op zoek gaat naar opvallende patronen en verbanden?
Krijg jij energie van het ontrafelen van complexe vraagstukken, het ontdekken van inzichten en het vertalen van data naar betekenisvolle resultaten? 

Dit is jouw uitdaging 

Het CBS ontvangt maandelijks van de 342 gemeenten in Nederland informatie over verleende bouwvergunningen. Gemeenten leveren deze gegevens aan via enquêtes en registreren de bouwvergunningen daarnaast in de Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen (BAG). 

Sinds 2025 publiceert het CBS de cijfers over bouwvergunningen op basis van de BAG. Er is echter een groot en toenemend verschil tussen de cijfers uit de BAG en de tellingen uit de enquêtes. Er is reeds onderzoek gedaan naar deze toenemende verschillen. 

Als stagiair ga je dit verder onderzoeken, door middel van een diepgaande analyse van de tijdigheid en kwaliteit van de registratie van gegevens in de BAG. Daarnaast verzamel je informatie over het registratieproces om beter inzicht te krijgen in hoe de BAG zich verhoudt tot de werkelijkheid. 

Je onderzoekt onder andere: 

- Hoe lang wachten gemeenten met registraties? 

- Worden registraties doorlopend geregistreerd, of opgespaard en in korte tijd geregistreerd in de BAG? 

- Verandert de kwaliteit en tijdigheid door de tijd heen? 

Om deze vragen te beantwoorden duik je in een grote database, waar je met behulp van SQL en R of Python trends gaat waarnemen, data visualiseert, en samenvattingen maakt. 

Daarnaast verzamel je informatie over het registratieproces, en hoe dit is geïmplementeerd bij gemeenten. Voor deze taak is al eerder onderzoek gedaan, en is er ook al meer informatie beschikbaar. Je verzamelt deze resultaten in een rapport met een overzicht van de huidige stand van zaken. 

Dit is jouw stageplek bij CBS Den Haag 

Ons team bestaat uit 24 enthousiaste collega’s, die met veel passie en plezier werken aan statistische informatie over vastgoed en de woningmarkt. 

We maken statistieken over (bouw)vergunningen, ontwikkeling van de woningvoorraad, (gemiddelde) WOZ-waardes, eigendomsverhoudingen, tijdelijke woningen, woningtransformaties en nog heel veel meer. We doen statistisch onderzoek op verzoek van organisaties in de publieke sector. En we beheren en verwerken data voor CBS-collega’s en werken samen met diverse organisaties, waaronder het Kadaster, de ministeries van BZK, VRO en EZK en Eurostat. 

We publiceren regelmatig over de dynamiek van de Nederlandse vastgoed- en woningmarkt. Onze nieuwsberichten halen regelmatig journaals, nieuwssites en voorpagina’s van landelijke dagbladen. En daar zijn we trots op! 

Dit breng jij mee 

Je volgt een hbo opleiding in de studierichting toegepaste wiskunde, data science of sociale wetenschappen. 

- Je hebt affiniteit met de woningmarkt. 

- Je hebt kennis en wellicht ervaring met R/rmarkdown en/of Python en SQL databases. 

- Je bent nieuwsgierig, leergierig en enthousiast om met data aan de slag te gaan. 

- Je vindt het leuk om nieuwe dingen te ontdekken, neemt graag initiatief en denkt actief mee. 

- Je kunt zelfstandig werken, maar zoekt ook graag de samenwerking op. 

- Je deelt gemakkelijk je ideeën en bevindingen en staat open voor nieuwe inzichten en feedback. 

Omdat tijdens de stage alle communicatie – zowel mondeling als schriftelijk – in het Nederlands plaatsvindt, is een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal noodzakelijk. 

Dit kun je van ons verwachten 

Een fijne leeromgeving waarin je: 

- samenwerkt met ervaren experts binnen hun vakgebied; 

- gaat werken met grote databases (SQL); 

- kennis opbouwt van de BAG en het registratieproces bij bronhouders; 

- analyses samenvat in data visualisaties en overzichtelijke tabellen. 

Voor jouw inzet ontvang je een stagevergoeding van € 800,- bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur per week). 

Samen met je stagebegeleider stem je af hoe je hybride kunt werken, met flexibele werktijden en de optie om deels vanuit huis aan jouw stageopdracht te werken. 

Dit zijn onze voorwaarden 

Het betreft een stageopdracht en geen werkervaringsplek. Voordat je aan de stage begint verwachten we dat je vanuit de onderwijsinstelling een stagebegeleider hebt, waarmee de stage is afgestemd en concrete leerdoelen zijn afgesproken. 
Deze stageopdracht is bedoeld voor studenten die momenteel staan ingeschreven bij een onderwijsinstelling; afgestudeerden komen niet in aanmerking.

title: Ingénieur ou post-doctorant pour l'analyse des données acquises par un radar HF océanographique couvrant le Raz Blanchard
company: ECOLE NATIONALE SUPERIEURE DE TECHNIQUES AVANCEES
description:
ENSTA, établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées, développe des activités de formation, de recherche et d’innovation dans les domaines de la défense et de la sécurité, des transports, de l'énergie, des activités maritimes, du numérique et de la santé.

L’école, présente sur deux campus, à Paris-Saclay et à Brest, est membre de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Classée dans le Top 10 des meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France, elle a pour mission :

- la formation d’élèves ingénieurs civils et militaires, de cadres et docteurs pour les secteurs public et privé,

- la recherche et l’innovation de haut niveau en relation étroite avec l’industrie des grands secteurs de souveraineté au sein de 6 unités de formation et de recherche (UFR).

Le/la titulaire du poste sera affecté au sein de l’UFR S2I sur le Campus de Brest.

Projet FLOWATT 

Le projet FLOWATT, dans le cadre duquel s’inscrit cette étude, vise à déployer et exploiter six hydroliennes dans les forts courants marins du Raz Blanchard, en Normandie.

Au-delà de la production d’énergie, FLOWATT a pour objectif d’évaluer le potentiel du Raz Blanchard pour le déploiement de fermes hydroliennes à plus grande échelle. Cette évaluation repose notamment sur une caractérisation précise de la ressource, une estimation fine du productible et une meilleure compréhension des impacts environnementaux. Pour répondre à ces enjeux, le projet combine mesures in situ, modélisation numérique et essais expérimentaux afin de fournir les connaissances nécessaires à la préparation des futurs déploiements commerciaux, tout en contribuant à la réduction des coûts de production et à la limitation des impacts sur l’environnement marin.

Dans ce contexte, la caractérisation de l’état de mer constitue un enjeu important, notamment dans une zone soumise à des courants très intenses. La présente étude s’intéresse ainsi aux données de radar HF acquises depuis fin 2017, ainsi qu’à celles qui seront nouvellement enregistrées dans le cadre du projet TidalRace. Le système, de technologie WERA, est réparti sur deux sites distants d’environ 5 km au Cap de la Hague et fonctionne à deux fréquences, 13,5 MHz et 24,5 MHz. Les acquisitions sont réalisées en continu, à raison de quatre mesures par heure, 24 h/24 et 7 j/7, sur une emprise couvrant l’ensemble du Raz Blanchard. Cette couverture temporelle et spatiale offre ainsi une opportunité unique de suivre l’évolution des états de mer dans des conditions hydrodynamiques particulièrement contraintes.

L’exploitation de ces données nécessite toutefois d’adapter les méthodes de traitement aux conditions de forts courants. L’objectif des travaux est donc d’améliorer les algorithmes existants et, si nécessaire, d’en développer de nouveaux afin de restituer de manière fiable les spectres d’énergie des vagues en fréquence et en direction, ainsi que les paramètres moyens associés. Une première étape consistera à comprendre les limites des méthodes actuelles, qui ne permettent plus de restituer un état de mer cohérent avec les références disponibles lorsque la vitesse du courant dépasse 1 m/s, comme montré par Lopez et al. (2018). Les méthodes développées seront ensuite évaluées à partir des mesures in situ et des modélisations numériques. Le radar HF constitue ainsi un élément central de ce travail, dont l’amélioration doit permettre de mieux caractériser les états de mer dans les forts courants du Raz Blanchard . 

Missions / Activités principales : 

Le (la) titulaire du poste sera affecté à l’équipe M3 de l’UMR Lab-STICC et sera en charge des missions principales suivantes :

- Réaliser une étude bibliographique sur les modèles permettant de décrire l’effet des vagues sur le spectre Doppler mesuré par un radar HF

- Implémenter un code de simulation intégrant l’effet des vagues à partir d’une description de l’état de mer dans le spectre Doppler

- Analyser les simulations en les comparant aux mesures réelles pour comprendre l’influence du courant et plus particulièrement des forts courants sur la mesure d’états de mer

- Proposer et implémenter des évolutions des algorithmes permettant de s’adapter aux forts courants présents sur la zone du Raz Blanchard

Missions / Activité annexe : 

- Participer à la démarche Qualité de l’établissement

- Contribuer à la démarche RSE dans le cadre de ses missions et de ses activités au sein de l’Ecole 

Niveau de diplôme et formations 

Les candidats doivent être titulaires d’un doctorat et/ou d’un diplôme d’ingénieur avec expérience dans un domaine pertinent (océanographie physique côtière, traitement du signal, etc…)

Emploi 

Postes ouverts aux candidats : 

- Agent contractuel

Durée d’affectation souhaitée : 18 mois 

Date de prise de fonctions prévue : 1er janvier 2027 

Rémunération : 

- Contractuels : en fonction de l'expérience professionnelle sur des postes de niveau équivalent

Lieu de travail : 

ENSTA Campus de Brest, 2 rue François Verny, 29200 BREST

« Le site est accessible en voiture (parking pour le personnel) ou en transports en commun. L’Ecole étant engagée dans une démarche RSE (DD-RS et employeur pro-vélo), elle encourage aux mobilités douces par la mise en place de dispositif d’aide financière (FMD) et des infrastructures adaptées aux cyclistes ».

Poste à temps complet (25 jours de congés annuels, 23 RTT annuels)

Avantages : 

- Transports (participation forfaitaire de l’employeur à hauteur de 75 %)

- Forfait mobilité durable (jusqu’à 300€/an)

- Possibilité de télétravail (après période d’essai et après accord du manager et dépôt d’une demande)

- Subvention employeur au restaurant administratif et/ou à la cafétéria de l’établissement

- Comité d’action sociale, avec notamment des événements et animations proposés au personnel, salle de sport sur adhésion,

- Mutuelle (participation à hauteur de 50% de l’établissement)

Aménagement du poste de travail et recrutement inclusif :

Tous nos postes sont ouverts aux candidats en situation de handicap.

ENSTA s’engage à un recrutement favorisant l’égalité, la diversité et l’inclusion. Toutes les candidatures sans aucune distinction (âge, handicap, sexe, nationalité, religion, orientation sexuelle…) ont leur place dans notre processus de recrutement.

Modalités de candidature 

- Un CV détaillé

- Une lettre de motivation décrivant votre profil et expliquant votre motivation et votre aptitude à occuper ce poste

- Une ou plusieurs lettres de recommandation

Envoyer les documents à guillaume SICOT ( 

Présentation de l’Ecole 

ENSTA est membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris) . Dans le cadre d’IP Paris, l’école participe aux activités des centres interdisciplinaires notamment du centre interdisciplinaire d'études pour la Défense et la Sécurité (CIEDS, soutenu par le ministère des armées et l’agence de l’innovation de défense (AID). Elle est à l’origine de la création du Centre interdisciplinaire Mers & Océans , inauguré en janvier 2025. Des chercheurs de l’école travaillent également en collaboration dans le cadre d'études portées par les centres Hi-Paris, lauréat en 2024 IA Cluster, E4C ou E4H notamment.

ENSTA résulte de la fusion le 1er janvier 2025 d’ENSTA Paris et d’ENSTA Bretagne. Son siège est situé à Palaiseau (91), sur le campus de Paris-Saclay et elle a un autre campus à Brest. Elle met en place une nouvelle formation d’ingénieur unifiée sur les deux campus (Paris-Saclay et Brest) à la rentrée académique 2026/2027.

Rejoindre l'école, c'est intégrer un établissement engagé pour la parité et l'égalité professionnelle, la diversité et l'accompagnement de ses agents en situation de handicap , dès le recrutement et tout au long de la carrière. Afin de préserver le bien-être au travail, l'école mène une politique active en matière de conditions de travail, reposant notamment sur un juste équilibre entre vie personnelle et vie professionnelle.

Connaissances : 

- Expérience dans la mesure de grandeurs océanographiques : 

- Connaissance en traitement du signal et/ou océanographique physique côtière

- Expérience en développement informatique : 

- Principalement en Python, des connaissances en C ou Fortran serait un plus

- Connaissance de Git

Savoir-faire: 

- Rédaction de rapports scientifiques et techniques en anglais

- Préparation et présentation d’exposés scientifiques en anglais

Aptitudes: 

- Autonomie

- Capacité à travailler en équipe

- Approche proactive

title: Forward Deployed Engineer - Software Engineer - Mexico
description:
About ElevenLabs


ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.


We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.


We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:



- 
ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.




- 
ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.




- 
ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.





Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




How we work



- 
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.




- 
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.




- 
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.




- 
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.




- 
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.





What we offer



- 
Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.




- 
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.




- 
Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.




- 
Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.




- 
Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.




- 
Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.





This role is remote, so it can be executed globally. 


About the role 


You’ll use your creativity, problem-solving, and technical expertise to design tailored solutions that make a real impact.


Embedded with our most strategic customers, you’ll get a front-row seat to some of our highest-stakes projects. From brainstorming technical architectures and product features to building full-scale integrations, you’ll take full ownership of complex, high-impact challenges—helping clients achieve their goals and push the limits of what’s possible.


What you will do:



- 
Take full ownership of end-to-end execution of major projects for our most strategic partners, working hands-on to deliver high-impact solutions.




- 
Collaborate daily with our customer’s engineers and executives teams to ensure the best use of ElevenLabs’ technologies.




- 
Drive real innovation by using your coding and technical skills to solve complex problems, making a real difference for our customers.





Requirements 



- 
Experience working with customers. It’s ok if you only worked with customers in student clubs or side projects, as long as you are interested in working closely with them on a technical capacity




- 
Proficiency in Python and strong software development knowledge, inclusive of a deep understanding of software development, software architecture, and APIs integration.




- 
Excellent communication and problem-solving skills. Especially in terms of ability to summarize complex technical knowledge and using logic in pursuing optimal solutions.





Location 



- 
This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Mexico, with a preference of Mexico City. Expect regular travel for customer onsites. Fluency in English and Spanish and a deep understanding of the regional and cultural nuances is required.





We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

title: Robotic Controls Engineer
description:
About Enact 

The next defining technological breakthrough will be in the physical world. We stand at a historical inflection point: bringing general-purpose intelligence into robotics.

At Enact we rethink the entire robotic tech stack from model architectures and data pipelines, to the actuators and sensors that feed the model. Pushing beyond pure vision and language approaches, we build a proprioceptive nerve system, and the cortex that makes sense of it, to solve dexterity through whole-body force-awareness and deploy robots for thousands of tasks in industry and beyond.

We are shaping a company where brilliant and unconventional people thrive together on solving the hardest challenges of our time. We are truth seekers. We reason from first principles, test our beliefs against reality, and trust that the best ideas can come from anyone. We move fast. We care deeply about our work and colleagues and are driven by passion to change the status quo.

If this resonates, we're excited to hear from you.

In This Role 

You will develop the proprioceptive motion control layer to enable our robots to do high contact manipulation predictably, smoothly, and safely under varied and uncertain conditions.

- Design and implement model- and learning-based estimation and control algorithms, along with the runtime loops that form the backbone for teleoperation and our AI-driven manipulation, from simulation to the real robot system.

- Debug and diagnose complex system behaviors spanning the interplay of hardware, software, and algorithms.

- Own robot bring-up, including validation and refinement of our robot model descriptions (URDF, MuJoCo XML, USD, etc.) for simulation and control, characterizing and adjusting for the sim-to-real gap as needed.

- Work together with both our hardware team and our AI researchers to continuously assess and push the performance of our full stack robot system

What We're Looking For 

- Degree (BSc/MSc/PhD) in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field

- Excellent theoretical and practical grasp of model and learning based whole-body control and state estimation

- Experience with robot simulation environments (MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or similar) and robot description files (URDF, USD, etc.)

- Proven ability to take complex algorithms from concept through hardware integration to production-ready real-time robot software

- Strong proficiency in Python, complemented by efficient low-level programming skills in Rust or C/C++

Bonus Points If You Have 

- Hands-on experience with tensor and automatic differentiation frameworks such as JAX, PyTorch, CppAD, Burn, or similar.

- Experience with whole-body force estimation

- Experience in developing reinforcement learning based robot control

- Experience in robot safety, including Control Barrier Functions and/or relevant industry certifications.

- Experience in contact rich manipulation, preferably including teleoperation and interfacing with large behavior models such as VLAs.

What we offer 

- The opportunity to make a real impact working on some of the biggest challenges of our time

- A fast-paced learning environment alongside an outstanding, driven team

- Ownership from day one, with the ability to iterate quickly and see your impact firsthand in an early-stage startup

- Visa sponsorship & relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

- A world-class in-person setup in central Zürich, with excellent prototyping, robotics, and technical infrastructure for hands-on builders

- Competitive compensation and meaningful equity participation
