title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Planning & Navigation)
description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will make our robots navigate dependably across real customer sites. Our stack works. The gap between working and dependable is the whole job. Every new site tests how a robot understands its surroundings and chooses where to go: a ramp the planner avoids, a narrow passage that exposes a poor route, a gate that changes the map, a person who steps into the robot's path, or localization drift that builds over a long patrol. You treat those cases as the real navigation problem to solve, not as edge cases.

You'll shape the technical choices behind reliable navigation, from sensor selection, ground segmentation, and traversability estimation to predicting how people and vehicles move and planning safe, efficient routes around them. The system has to work day and night, in challenging weather, across different embodiments and changing site conditions. We measure success by whether the robot completes its patrol on a live site, not by how it performs in simulation.

What You'll Work On

- Navigation and path-planning design: how robots represent traversable space, select routes, avoid obstacles, and reach goals across complex sites.

- Sensor integration driven by navigation requirements, including what ground segmentation and traversability estimation need in day, night, and challenging weather.

- Environment understanding: how the robot distinguishes ground from obstacles and estimates which terrain is safe and practical to traverse.

- Behavior prediction: anticipate how people, vehicles, and other dynamic obstacles will move, and plan routes that stay safe and efficient around them.

- Field reliability: reproduce failures from deployments, find the root cause, and fix it at the right layer, from sensor data and maps to costmaps, planners, and recovery behaviors.

- Planning under imperfect localization: plans that stay useful when the state estimate drifts and the robot must execute routes in tight or dynamic environments, working with the rest of Robot Autonomy on localization and control.

- Validation on real robots: logs, simulation, and repeatable field tests to verify that design choices and changes hold across routes, lighting, weather, and site layouts.

- New autonomy capabilities: work with the engineers building the operator application and backend so operator requests and new robot capabilities rest on a sound navigation design.

- The field feedback loop: work closely with forward-deployed engineers to turn site issues into bugs, design changes, and improvements to the navigation stack.

- Regular site visits to build a practical understanding of how robots and sensors behave in real operating conditions.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for an engineer who has taken a robotics system from unreliable to dependable and takes ownership beyond individual tickets. You can explain why you made a navigation design choice and what it costs. When a robot takes a bad route, you can tell whether the planner, the map, the state estimate, or the robot's behavior is at fault, and you fix the right one. You are comfortable in the field and want to understand how robots behave in real customer environments.

Your Background

- A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Proven track record building and deploying navigation on ground mobile robots in the real world (3+ years or equivalent depth).

- Hands-on experience with mobile robot navigation and path planning: route or local planning, static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, costmaps, or recovery behaviors.

- Understanding of how mapping and localization affect navigation, and the ability to diagnose when a planning issue is actually caused by the map, the state estimate, or robot behavior.

- Understanding of how lighting, weather, terrain, and sensor limitations affect perception and navigation, with experience developing or validating systems for demanding real-world conditions.

- Hands-on experience with robotics sensors and hardware, especially LiDAR, IMUs, and cameras. You can investigate issues across software, networking, and hardware boundaries.

- Experience testing and debugging navigation on physical robots using logs, visualization, simulation, and repeatable field tests.

- Strong ROS 2, C++, and Python skills.

- Clear communication of navigation and path-planning design choices and their trade-offs.

- Willingness to visit customer sites regularly.

Nice to Have

- Experience with legged robots or with more than one robot embodiment.

- Experience with Nav2 or a comparable navigation framework.

- Motion prediction or planning among people and vehicles, such as trajectory forecasting or socially aware navigation.

- Terrain mapping and traversability methods: elevation mapping, learned traversability, or semantic segmentation for navigation.

- Experience with night-time or all-weather sensing, such as thermal cameras or LiDAR in rain and fog.

- Background in security, defence, or other safety-critical robotics deployments.

What We Offer

- Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

- Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

- Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

- Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

- Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

- Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

description:
Why Mozilla ? 

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. 

About this team and role: 

The JavaScript team at Mozilla works to make Firefox's industry-leading JavaScript engine SpiderMonkey even more performant. We push the boundaries of what the web is capable of, shaping the future of the JavaScript language through standardization at TC39, while keeping in mind the fundamental principle of “don’t break the web.”

As a Staff Software Engineer on the SpiderMonkey team, you'll be a domain expert who drives the engine's runtime performance forward, from the interpreter and JITs to the garbage collector, while also helping maintain and advance the health of a large, mature C++ codebase. You'll typically lead performance projects within the team, planning the work and mitigating the risk yourself, and you'll mentor other engineers as you take on increasingly ambiguous, high-impact problems.

What you’ll do: 

- Lead runtime performance initiatives: Own projects to improve SpiderMonkey's runtime performance, from profiling and identifying bottlenecks to designing and landing optimizations across the interpreter, JITs, and garbage collector.

- Provide technical leadership to the team: Mitigate risk for the performance projects you own, planning work that may start out ambiguous and require significant up-front design and prototyping.

- Maintain and advance the codebase: Help preserve the correctness and stability of a large, mature C++ codebase while improving its architecture and maintainability as the JavaScript language and the engine continue to evolve.

- Track and shape the JavaScript standard: Work with the JavaScript team to keep up with the evolving TC39 standard, and help evaluate proposals where performance or implementation tradeoffs are involved.

- Strengthen engine security: Collaborate with the Fuzzing team to identify and close security issues in the JavaScript engine.

- Mentor and elevate the team: Mentor other engineers by stewarding some of your existing responsibilities to more junior team members as you take on new, larger initiatives, and help the team build stronger performance-analysis and benchmarking practices.

- Communicate clearly: Turn team strategy and goals into concrete action for the projects you lead, and communicate progress, tradeoffs, and technical decisions clearly to your team and to partner teams.

- Use AI tools day to day: Incorporate AI-assisted tools into your workflow for debugging, prototyping, code analysis, and development.

What you’ll bring: 

- 5+ years developing C++ applications

- Demonstrated expertise in systems programming, including direct experience with one or more of: compilers, garbage collectors, interpreters, and virtual machines

- Strong background in performance analysis, profiling, and benchmarking on large and complex software

- Experience with general systems architecture (x86, x64, ARM, ARM64, etc.)

- A track record of technical leadership: planning ambiguous projects, sequencing project work, and mitigating risk with minimal help

- Experience mentoring other engineers and helping raise a team's technical standards

- Creative problem solver with strong debugging skills and a detailed approach to code review

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable turning team strategy into action and communicating tradeoffs to peers

title: Stage Data Science & Clinical AI – start dec 2026 t/m mrt 2027
description:
Wil je meebouwen aan de zorg van morgen met AI? Als stagiair bij Pacmed bouw je modellen die de besluitvorming in Nederlandse ziekenhuizen elke dag verbeteren. Je werkt met echte klinische data, samen met data scientists, engineers en clinici. We zoeken twee stagiairs die starten tussen december 2026 en maart 2027.

Over Pacmed 

Bij Pacmed combineren we technologie en menselijkheid om de zorg toegankelijk en toekomstbestendig te houden. Onze software draait al in meerdere Nederlandse ziekenhuizen en we breiden actief verder uit. We helpen zorgprofessionals om real-time betere beslissingen te nemen, capaciteit efficiënter te benutten en patiëntenstromen soepel te laten verlopen. Als stagiair zit je precies op het punt waar onze modellen en data de klinische praktijk raken.

Waarom Pacmed een ideale stageplek is:

- We zijn een scale-up met een duidelijke missie: de zorg toegankelijk en toekomstbestendig houden.

- Je werk doet ertoe. Het komt terecht in producten die in ziekenhuizen gebruikt worden, niet in een la.

- Je krijgt een begeleider die investeert in je ontwikkeling, en een team dat elkaar graag beter maakt.

- We gaan vriendelijk en respectvol met elkaar om en hebben graag plezier, met regelmatige teamuitjes en een jaarlijkse off-site.

De twee stages 

Elke stagiair krijgt een eigen project. Beide projecten gaan over patiëntenstromen: hoeveel patiënten komen het ziekenhuis binnen, en hoeveel stromen er uit naar de nazorg.

Stage 1: instroom voorspellen op de acute as (Capaciteitsmonitor) 

De Pacmed Capaciteitsmonitor geeft zorgprofessionals AI-voorspellingen op basis van real-time ziekenhuisdata, zodat ze personeel en capaciteit proactief kunnen plannen in plaats van reactief. De capaciteitsmonitor voorspelt patiëntbezetting en zorgzwaarte en vertaalt dat naar de daadwerkelijk benodigde personele capaciteit.

We breiden deze aanpak nu uit naar andere afdelingen op de acute as: de spoedeisende hulp (SEH), de eerste harthulp (EHH) en de cardiac care unit (CCU). Daar houdt de personeelsplanning nog weinig rekening met schommelingen in de instroom, met over- en onderbezetting als gevolg.

Sinds september 2026 werkt een stagiair aan instroommodellen voor deze afdelingen. Jij versterkt dat project en bouwt erop voort. Denk aan:

- modellen voor de SEH, EHH en CCU ontwikkelen en verbeteren op basis van ziekenhuisdata over instroom, uitstroom en bezetting en publieke data zoals weer, evenementen en epidemiologische gegevens

- de (potentiële) impact van de AI modellen op de personeelsplanning doorrekenen

- afdelingen (SEH, EHH, CCU) of ziekenhuizen met elkaar vergelijken;

- de uitkomsten samen met clinici interpreteren en valideren.

Stage 2: uitstroom naar de VVT voorspellen (Transfer Monitor) 

De Pacmed Transfer Monitor richt zich op een van de grotere inefficiënties in Nederlandse ziekenhuizen: vertraagde overplaatsing van patiënten naar de nazorg. Patiënten die medisch gezien niet meer in het ziekenhuis hoeven te liggen maar nog nergens terechtkunnen ("verkeerde bedden") zijn naar schatting goed voor 5 tot 15% van de ligdagen in de ziekenhuizen waarmee we werken. Dat blokkeert de doorstroom vanaf bijvoorbeeld de SEH en het electieve programma, is vervelend voor patiënten, verhoogt het risico op complicaties en kost onnodig geld.

De Transfer Monitor voorspelt vroeg en per patiënt of iemand nazorg nodig heeft en wat de verwachte ontslagdatum is. Zo kan het transferbureau bepalen welke patiënten het eerst gescreend worden, en kunnen artsen en verpleegkundigen het ontslag op tijd regelen.

In deze stage gebruik je klinische data om te voorspellen hoeveel patiënten uitstromen naar VVT-instellingen (verpleeg- en verzorgingshuizen en thuiszorg). Daarmee kunnen die instellingen hun eigen capaciteit beter plannen. Je bouwt en evalueert het model en toetst het samen met ziekenhuizen en nazorginstellingen.

Wat ga je doen?

- Je traint en evalueert machine-learningmodellen op echte ziekenhuisdata.

- Je ontwerpt en voert impactanalyses uit die de klinische waarde van onze producten laten zien en verbeteren.

- Je schuift aan bij sessies met clinici om hun werkproces te begrijpen en dat te vertalen naar modelkeuzes.

Wat bieden we 

Je krijgt intensieve begeleiding van een ervaren data scientist, met echte ruimte om je project zelf te trekken. Je bouwt een stevig portfolioproject op een echt clinical-AI-probleem, en de stage richten we zo in dat hij past bij de eisen van je scriptie of opleiding. Vanaf dag één hoor je er volwaardig bij. Eerdere stagiairs leverden werk op dat direct in onze producten terechtkwam, zoals ons zorgzwaartemodel.

Daarnaast:

- een stagevergoeding van €500 per maand;

- regelmatige sociale activiteiten, met kwartaaluitjes en een jaarlijkse off-site;

- flexibele werktijden en de mogelijkheid om af en toe vanuit het buitenland te werken;

- 25 vakantiedagen per jaar op basis van een fulltime dienstverband (naar rato bij parttime);

- dagelijks lunch op kantoor, met veel vegetarische en veganistische opties;

- de mogelijkheid om standaard feestdagen te ruilen voor andere dagen, bijvoorbeeld voor persoonlijke of religieuze feestdagen;

- een laptop van de zaak voor de duur van je stage.

Solliciteren 

De sollicitatie bestaat uit een of twee gesprekken waarbij we kennis maken, jij de kans krijgt om je vragen te stellen en wij graag meer horen over je motivatie en ervaring.

Interesse? Stuur ons een korte motivatie en je cv. Vermeld je opleiding, je beschikbaarheid (startdatum en aantal uur per week) en of je een voorkeur hebt voor stage 1 of stage 2.

Wie zoeken we 

We zoeken iemand die analyses kan uitvoeren, modellen kan bouwen en de uitkomsten hervan op een begrijpelijke manier kan presenteren en bespreken met clinici zonder data-achtergrond. Dit vragen we:

- Je spreekt Nederlands. Je werkt met personeelsplanners, verpleegkundig teamleiders, capaciteits- en transfermedewerkers in Nederlandse ziekenhuizen, en met Nederlandstalige data.

- Je hebt een goede data science-achtergrond. Je beheerst de kernprincipes en kunt in Python zelfstandig analyses uitvoeren en modellen bouwen, evalueren en verbeteren. Praktijkervaring, bijvoorbeeld uit een eerdere stage, baan of serieus project, heeft onze voorkeur.

- De stage is onderdeel van je masteropleiding of promotietraject.

- Je kunt starten tussen december 2026 en maart 2027.

- Je bent minimaal 6 maanden fulltime beschikbaar, of een gelijkwaardige hoeveelheid tijd parttime (meer dan 50% van fulltime, over een navenant langere periode).

Klinische ervaring is een pre, bijvoorbeeld als (bijna) laborant, verpleegkundige of technisch geneeskundige of vanuit een bijbaan. Het helpt je om de data goed te interpreteren en om de juiste vragen te stellen aan de mensen die onze producten gebruiken.

Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you own our customer deployments end to end. Our system runs on-prem at industrial facilities, critical infrastructure, and military sites, integrated with the cameras, networks, and robots already in place. You survey the site, plan the deployment, install and integrate the system, tune it to the site's conditions, and hand it over to operators who will rely on it daily.

You are also the technical face of Laelaps on site. You work with security operators to understand how they actually work and where the bottlenecks are, align with their leadership on what success looks like, and translate what you learn into configuration, code, and product priorities. Early deployments you run alongside the founders; over time you own sites and accounts independently.

Expect roughly half your time at customer sites in Switzerland and Europe, and the rest in Zurich, turning field lessons into tooling and automation that make each deployment faster than the last. This is an engineering role with a customer in the room, not a support or services role.

What You'll Work On

- Deployments end-to-end: site surveys, network and hardware planning, installation, camera and VMS integration, commissioning, validation, and handover.

- On-prem infrastructure: install and manage our stack on edge hardware (NVIDIA DGX Spark, Jetson Thor class devices) inside customer networks, often air-gapped or heavily restricted.

- Integrations: connect existing cameras, sensors, VMS platforms, and robots into one coordinated system, and write the glue code where no integration exists yet.

- System tuning: calibrate detection and tracking to each site's terrain, lighting, and threat profile until the system performs in the field as it does in the demo.

- Pilots to production: make POCs succeed technically, because pilots that work become contracts.

- Customer understanding: sit with operators, interview stakeholders from the control room to the leadership floor, and map the real problems and bottlenecks behind the stated requirements.

- Customer trust: train operators, respond fast when something breaks, and be the engineer customers ask for by name.

- The deployment playbook: turn every hard-won lesson into runbooks, tooling, and automation that compound.

- Product feedback: bring real field signal back to the core engineering team and shape the roadmap with it.

Who We're Looking For

We are looking for an engineer who runs toward the messy parts, with the EQ to match the IQ. You are as comfortable in a server room or on a windswept perimeter as you are in a terminal, and just as comfortable in a conversation. You can spend a shift with a security operator and earn enough trust that they tell you what actually goes wrong at 3 a.m., then brief a head of security or a site director in their language, not yours. You listen more than you pitch, you read the room, and you switch registers between the guard house and the boardroom without breaking stride. You debug across the whole stack without ceremony: is it the hardware, the network, the driver, the model, or the config? Above all, you take personal ownership of the outcome: the deployment works because you made it work, and the customer trusts us because you earned it.

Your Background

- 3+ years of relevant software, robotics, embedded systems, or systems integration experience.

- A Master’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Strong Python and hands-on C++ experience. You can read, debug, and extend production code in both.

- Experience deploying and operating software on-prem or at the edge (Docker required; GPU inference experience a strong plus).

- Experience working with sensors and embedded systems, including device interfaces and communications protocols.

- High EQ and experience working directly with end users or customers: you can uncover needs, work across stakeholders, and communicate technical issues clearly.

- Composure in customer-facing technical sessions, including when systems fail and plans need to change.

- Fluent German and/or French, and good English. Our sites and their operators run in German; the team runs in English.

- Willingness to travel regularly to customer sites across Switzerland and Europe, with multi-day on-site stints.

- Based in or willing to relocate to Zurich.

- Citizenship of Switzerland, an EU/EFTA member state, or a NATO member state, and eligibility for security clearance where customer sites require it.

- A valid category B driving license.

Nice to Have

- Real networking competence: VLANs, firewalls, routing, VPNs, and debugging connectivity in networks you do not control.

- Hands-on comfort with hardware: you have racked servers, flashed devices, crimped a cable, or built systems that touch the physical world. Checking cable connections at 2 a.m. at a client site is second nature while debugging an issue on a customer side.

- Experience with cameras, VMS platforms (Milestone, Genetec, or similar), ONVIF/RTSP, or the physical security industry.

- Computer vision or ML deployment experience, especially optimising inference on edge GPUs.

- Robotics experience: ROS2 and Rviz2, robot integration, or fleet operations.

- Experience in defence, government, or other regulated environments.

- French, Italian, or another European language.

- Startup experience, ideally somewhere you were handed a hard problem and a deadline instead of a spec.

What We Offer

- Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

- Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

- Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

- Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

- Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

- Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

Hong Kong

Core Responsibilities
AI & GPU Infrastructure Management: Provision, monitor, and scale high-performance GPU clusters (NVIDIA H100/A100, CUDA/ROCm setups) for heavy model training and inference workloads.

Containerization & Orchestration: Deploy, scale, and manage distributed containerized workloads using Kubernetes (K8s), Docker, and KubeFlow or Ray.
Observability & Reliability: Implement logging, tracing, and metric dashboards (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry) to track cluster health, GPU memory/utilization, and inference latency.
Security & Governance: Enforce DevSecOps practices, secret management (HashiCorp Vault), container image scanning, and access controls tailored for sensitive AI datasets and models.

Experience: 3+ years of experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), or Cloud/Platform Engineering, with exposure to MLOps or AI/ML workloads.
Cloud & Containers: Strong hands-on experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure, alongside production Kubernetes and Docker management.
Scripting & Programming: Proficiency in Python, Bash/Shell, or Go for automation and tooling.
IaC & CI/CD: Demonstrated mastery of Terraform, GitOps workflows, and automated testing/deployment pipelines.
AI Ecosystem Knowledge: Familiarity with GPU node provisioning, distributed storage for massive datasets, and model serving runtimes.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with LLM orchestration frameworks (LangChain, Ray Serve, vLLM).
Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.

Apply today and find plenty of reasons to SMILE! 

The Cloud Engineer (Automation) is responsible for designing, building, operating and improving production-grade automation for Smile Digital Health, its clients and partners. This role will be responsible for the pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and recovery procedures, that the platform runs on. 

This Engineer will merge direct platform engineering expertise with driving strategic changes in how the department designs, deploys, and maintains its infrastructure. Key responsibilities include managing build and release engineering, orchestrating the Terraform and Helm infrastructure, provisioning on-demand environments, and implementing automated recovery. This role works closely with Platform Engineering, Solution Engineering, Service Operations and Engineering Practice & QA to remove unnecessary repetitive, manual work and effectively optimize a build from the time the client commits to a running environment faster, decrease platform costs, and utilize AI to enhance the platformâs engineering and operations.

\n 

Responsibilities: 

- Own build and release engineering by reviewing the current repositories and CI setup, then consolidate duplicated Azure DevOps pipeline YAML onto shared reusable templates with change detection and automated quality gates.

- Identify and eliminate manual efforts for cross-functional teams and replace them with scheduled, auditable automation. For example, automating patching, certificate and secret rotation, environment scaling, and recurring reports

- Implement GitOps-based continuous delivery - declarative, Git-driven deployments with automated reconciliation, drift detection and rollback.

- Automate line-of-business environments end to end, provisioned and torn down on demand across every Azure service and application involved.

- Automate business continuity and disaster recovery through backup validation, restore and failover, recurring DR drills, and measured RTO and RPO.

- Ensure Helm and Terraform are easy to upgrade by charting reuse and configuration validation, versioned modules, and state boundaries that limit how far an upgrade reaches.

- Run in-cluster platform services deployed through Helm, harden workloads for availability and capacity: health probes, replica counts, and right-sized requests, limits and autoscaling.

- Ensure that the Terraform configuration is regularly maintained.

- Build and maintain Build Agent images for streamlining tooling available for the builds. 

- Automate the guardrails such as policy-as-code, security and IaC scanning in the pipeline, and alerts and dashboards defined as code.

- Implement AI-assisted engineering in the platform teamâs day-to-day work

- Contribute to the departmentâs AI enablement, package knowledge into reusable skills and runbooks in the shared skill library.

- Work with the development and operations teams to find automation gaps, prioritize them, and close them.

- Troubleshoot production and staging issues and document what you automate so others can operate it.

Requirements: 

- 6+ years of hands-on cloud engineering, DevOps and/or platform engineering experience, including at least 1-2+ years with infrastructure as code and CI/CD automation on Microsoft Azure in production.

- Post-secondary education in Computer Science, Engineering, or similar and/or equivalent work experience. 

- Practical in-depth knowledge and expertise in Terraform, Helm and Azure DevOps pipelines, and GitOps delivery (Argo CD or Flux). 

- Strong Terraform skills including, but not limited to, experience with module design, provider version management, state management and refactoring.

- Expertise in Helm chart authoring and refactoring, including recent experience with Kubernetes and AKS.

- Demonstrated knowledge across Azure (AKS, Key Vault, Storage, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, networking, identity) and observability as code (Azure Monitor and/or Grafana, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry).

- Hands-on experience automating backup, restore and failover with measured RTO and RPO.

- Hands-on experience with agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent), keeping confidential data out of them and reviewing what they produce.

- Hands-on experience running, hardening and right-sizing production workloads on Kubernetes

- Hands-on Kafka operations: topic and partition design, consumer group sizing, and throughput and latency trade-offs. Experience migrating between Kafka platforms (HDInsight, Confluent, MSK or self-managed) is a strong asset.

- Strong Python and Bash skills, able to build maintainable tooling, not glue scripts.

- A demonstrable record of replacing manual processes with automation.

- FinOps practice and Azure Cost Management, an asset. 

- Regulated environment experience (healthcare, PHI), an asset. 

- Certifications: HashiCorp Terraform Associate; Microsoft AZ-104, AZ-400, AZ-305; CKA or CKAD, an asset. 

- Observability as code with Azure Monitor, Grafana, Prometheus, or OpenTelemetry; Azure cost optimization, an asset.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Go SDK - Language Clients
description:
About the team

The Integrations Ecosystem org builds the drivers, SDKs, connectors and BI integrations that make ClickHouse feel native in any stack. The Language Clients team maintains the official clients for Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust, C++ and C#, plus the ODBC, JDBC and ADBC drivers. We're small, senior and remote across North America and EMEA.

The role

We're looking for a product-minded engineer to own ClickHouse's Go clients. You'll decide what the clients should do by talking to the developers who use them, reading the issues and the telemetry, and listening to the community. Then you'll build it, with deep Go expertise, and measure whether it worked. Your scope is the SDK and what builds on it: clickhouse-go and ch-go, and the collectors, pipelines, agents and tools that write millions of rows per second through your code.

What you'll do

- Know who uses the clients and what they're trying to do. Define what good looks like (time to first query, error clarity, throughput, adoption by key integrations), measure it, and let that drive the roadmap.

- Be the voice of ClickHouse for Go developers. Speak at GopherCon and Go meetups, and write the posts, tutorials and examples that developers and AI assistants find when they search for how to use ClickHouse from Go (SEO and GEO). Answer questions where the community asks them.

- Own the Go clients and their ecosystem: clickhouse-go, ch-go, database/sql, releases and support. Evolve them without breaking the people who depend on them.

- Keep the clients the fastest Go option for the fastest analytical database, and make sure the client is never the bottleneck. Performance is part of every release, not an afterthought: profile, change, measure again, catch regressions in CI, and publish the numbers.

- Partner with the projects built on the clients, from the OpenTelemetry Collector to ClickHouse Grafana datasource and ClickPipes, and catch their regressions before they ship.

- Review and co-maintain other clients, and take part in cross-client decisions on types, errors and protocol features.

- Bring written proposals about where we invest next. You set direction rather than wait for it.

- Make the clients enterprise-ready: TLS and mTLS, cloud authentication, safe credential handling, vulnerability response, a small dependency footprint, and the questions large Go shops ask before they adopt.

- Shape the clients for agents as users: an API, docs and error messages an AI coding agent can use correctly on the first try.

- Extend our AI development platform, with new workflows for maintaining the clients: consistency checks across languages, issue triage, release checks.

About you

- Product-minded with a bias for action. You'd rather run an experiment and bring back data than wait for approval, you measure whether it worked, and you can explain what you chose not to build.

- 5+ years in software, much of it on data-intensive systems: drivers, SDKs, ingestion, streaming, observability or analytics.

- Deep Go expertise: the runtime and garbage collector, escape analysis, the memory model, pprof and the execution tracer. You reason about throughput and latency down to allocations and bytes on the wire, and you prove it with tests and benchmarks.

- Strong Go concurrency instincts: context, goroutines and channels, bounded pools, backpressure, clean shutdown, and the leaks and races that come with each.

- Beyond Go, productive in at least one more of our client languages (Python, JavaScript, Java, Rust, C++, C#). You'll review and co-own across clients.

- You've built or substantially extended a Go module other engineers depend on. You understand semantic import versioning and treat breaking changes accordingly.

- Strong grasp of database fundamentals: SQL, query execution and analytical workloads. Judgment about when to use database/sql and when to drop down to the protocol.

- Enthusiastic about working in public. You've given talks or written technical content, or you're keen to, and you see it as part of the job rather than a distraction from it.

- Thoughtful use of AI development tools, with the judgment to review what comes out.

- Clear writing. Most coordination happens in design docs, PRs and RFCs.

Nice to have

- ClickHouse, especially its type system and native format, or another columnar or OLAP engine.

- Contributions to Go data or observability infrastructure: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Kafka clients, database drivers.

- Building or maintaining a database/sql driver.

- Apache Arrow or ADBC in Go.

- Experience designing SDKs, docs or error messages with AI coding agents as the consumer.

- Protocol or wire-format work on a database driver or network client.

Learn more

- clickhouse-go on GitHub and ch-go on GitHub 

- ClickHouse Go client documentation 

- Chasing that 32 ms tail latency in ClickHouse 

Perks 

- Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

- Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

- Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

- Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

- A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

- Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

title: Research Engineer, Foundation Model (Multimodal Fusion & Distillation)
description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

You will build the parts of LEA, our foundation model of the physical world, where field data is the input. LEA takes in cameras, infrared, thermal, lidar and robot state natively, around the clock, on real security sites. We stand on the best open models for the encoders and the reasoning head and do not pretrain from scratch. Your work goes where nobody else can do it: fusing every sensor into one stream, teaching an open vision-language model to reason over that stream, and distilling a fast model that sees every frame.

This is the first engineer dedicated to the model track, so you will also set how we train, evaluate and ship models. You will work with our Command Centre and Robot Autonomy teams to get what you train running on site appliances and robots, and you will see it tested at 03:00 in the rain.

What You'll Work On

- Native encoders: adapt the best open vision and point-cloud foundation models to RGB, IR, thermal and lidar, one encoder per sensor, raw stream in.

- Fusion: build the layer that aligns every sensor in time and space into one token stream, trained on time-aligned multi-sensor field data that exists nowhere else.

- Slow head: fine-tune an open frontier vision-language model to reason over fused sensor tokens instead of pictures.

- Fast head: distil a small model from the slow head's calls on our own events, so every frame is seen and only hard cases escalate.

- Evaluation: held-out sites, night and thermal slices, regression gates. A model that is worse anywhere does not ship.

- Training machinery: multi-GPU training, data loaders for multi-sensor clips, experiment tracking and reproducible runs.

Who We're Looking For

A research engineer who has shipped multimodal models, not only published them. You know when an open model is good enough and when to build, you measure on the slice that matters before claiming a number, and you care whether the model works on a real site, not only on a benchmark.

Your Background

- 4+ years training and fine-tuning large vision or multimodal models, or a PhD plus industry experience.

- Strong PyTorch, comfortable with multi-GPU and multi-node training.

- Hands-on fine-tuning of vision-language models (instruction tuning, parameter-efficient methods, full fine-tunes).

- Experience with knowledge distillation or model compression for deployment.

- Work with video or non-RGB sensors: thermal, infrared, lidar or radar.

- Evaluation discipline and solid software engineering hygiene.

Nice to Have

- Point-cloud or 3D foundation models.

- Self-supervised and latent-prediction methods (JEPA-style).

- Edge deployment with TensorRT or similar.

- Robotics or field data collection.

- Publications at top ML, vision or robotics venues.

What We Offer

- Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

- Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

- Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

- Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

- Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

- Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer (Backend-oriented), Growth - Platform
description:
About CookUnity :

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About CookUnity

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul.

Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world. 

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About the Team:

Our Growth Platform team brings together Engagement and Accounts & Identity to build the experiences and technical foundations that help customers start, deepen, and renew their relationship with CookUnity.

On the Engagement side, we help new customers build lasting habits, keep active customers engaged, grow through referrals, and welcome back customers who have left. On the Accounts & Identity side, we own the services that power customer accounts, authentication, and secure access across our products, providing reliable capabilities that other engineering teams build upon.

Our work spans customer experiences across web and mobile, shared backend services, and the evolution of our platform into scalable, independent systems. We partner closely with Product, Design, Data, and Engineering to experiment, measure outcomes, and turn successful ideas into lasting capabilities. For engineers, this means combining direct customer impact with deep technical ownership, making CookUnity easier to use while helping teams across the company build and move faster.

The role:

As a Senior Full Stack Engineer (Backend oriented) on our Growth Platform team, you will help shape and own the core services behind Accounts & Identity, including authentication, user accounts, and the foundations of a shared notification system.

Working closely with our Staff Engineer, you will take ownership from technical design through implementation, rollout, and operation in production. You will evolve our authentication platform and User Service, build reliable integrations across services, and establish reusable capabilities that enable product teams to deliver timely, relevant notifications across channels.

This role calls for strong backend engineering expertise and sound judgment around distributed systems, database design, performance, and real-time and event-driven architectures. You should be comfortable investigating slow queries, designing APIs and asynchronous workflows, and making practical tradeoffs around consistency, scalability, security, and reliability.

You will partner with engineers across CookUnity to understand their needs and turn them into clear service boundaries and dependable integrations. Your impact will come from both delivering new capabilities and ensuring that the systems other teams depend on remain fast, observable, and easy to build upon.

Responsibilities: 

- Own the design, implementation, and operation of core backend services across authentication, identity, and user account management.

- Partner with our Staff Engineer to define technical direction, make architecture decisions, and deliver projects from discovery through production.

- Build the foundations of a shared notification system, including event processing, delivery workflows, and integrations with messaging providers.

- Design APIs and service integrations with clear contracts, reliable failure handling, and well-defined ownership.

- Improve performance and scalability through database design, query optimization, indexing, caching, and efficient data access patterns.

- Build asynchronous and real-time capabilities, accounting for retries, idempotency, ordering, and data consistency.

- Evolve legacy functionality into independent services, planning safe migrations that preserve data integrity and service availability.

- Protect customer data through secure authentication, authorization, and access management practices.

- Establish meaningful automated tests, observability, and rollout strategies, and participate in incident response and the on-call rotation.

- Collaborate with Product and Engineering teams to translate business needs into reusable platform capabilities, review code, and mentor other engineers.

Qualifications: 

- 5+ years of software engineering experience, with a strong focus on backend services and production systems.

- Strong backend development experience with both Kotlin/Java and Node.js with TypeScript, including building and operating production services. Deep expertise in at least one stack and the ability to contribute independently in the other.

- Solid knowledge of relational databases, including data modeling, indexing, query optimization, transactions, and safe schema migrations.

- Experience building distributed systems and asynchronous workflows, with an understanding of retries, idempotency, and data consistency.

- Experience diagnosing and improving backend performance using metrics, logs, traces, and profiling.

- Familiarity with authentication and authorization concepts, including OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, and secure session management.

- Experience integrating internal services and third-party APIs, with thoughtful handling of failures and service dependencies.

- A track record of owning projects from technical design through testing, deployment, and production support.

- Clear communication skills, advanced English, and the ability to collaborate on technical decisions and explain tradeoffs.

Benefits

💸 Get paid in USD

🗺 Work remotely: design the life that you want

⛱ Enjoy 15 days of vacation each year from the start date

🎄 16 fully paid Argentinean holidays

🩺 Healthcare Benefit: Monthly stipend to use in your preferred healthcare provider

🗓️ 5- year Sabbatical: After 5 years with CookUnity, you get a 4-week paid sabbatical

🐣 Paid Family leave

🕯 Compassionate Leave: 3-5 days each time the need arises

🧘🏽‍♀️ Customize the benefits that suit your needs! Access a range of perks tailored to you, including learning opportunities, wellness memberships, delivery apps, and more through our comprehensive benefit platform

🤖 AI-forward workplace: enterprise access to ChatGPT and Claude to help you work smarter and grow faster.

🧑‍🏫 Personalized English coach

If you’re interested in this role, please submit your application, and if we think you might be a fit, we'll get in touch with you. Thank you for your time! 

CookUnity is an Equal Opportunity Employer . We are dedicated to creating a community of inclusion and an environment free from discrimination or harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or physical or mental disability. 

A quick note for all candidates 
We’ve recently seen an increase in recruitment scams across the industry, and we want to make sure you (and your data) stay safe while applying to CookUnity. We also want you to know that we take this seriously — sometimes, as part of our process, we may ask for a brief “proof of humanity” to confirm that we’re connecting with a real person, not an impersonator. Here are a few tips to help you protect yourself and know what to expect from us: 

- Apply only through our official channels. All open roles are listed on our official careers page: careers.cookunity.com 

- Our recruiters are real people — and easy to verify. You can always find them on LinkedIn with verified profiles. If you’re unsure, feel free to reach out to us on our official LinkedIn Company Page . 

- We only communicate through official CookUnity channels. That means emails ending in @cookunity.com and interviews held through official company platforms (Google Meet or Zoom) — never WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS. 

- We’ll never ask for payment or personal financial details. If anyone does, please don’t share any information and let us know right away. 

If something ever feels off or you’re unsure about a message, we’d much rather you double-check with us. You can always contact us directly through any of our social media channels. We appreciate your interest in joining CookUnity — and we care about keeping your experience (and safety) as genuine as possible.

About the role: 

The OfferUp Connect team builds the moments that turn a listing into a sale. Every chat between buyers and sellers, every offer notification, and every saved-search alert runs through services we own, from messaging and notifications to location, meetups, and the subscriptions sellers pay for. We run high-volume Java microservices and streaming pipelines, integrate with partners like Braze, Amazon Pinpoint, Apple, and Google, and use experimentation to decide what ships.

We also take on high-visibility work beyond our domain. Connect built OfferUp's video infrastructure for listing videos and LLM-powered catalog enrichment on Amazon Bedrock, both company priorities that changed what buyers see every day. The roadmap is wide open for someone who wants to help shape it.

As a Software Development Engineer II, you'll own features from concept to rollout: designing and writing well-tested code, launching experiments, and measuring results with Product, Design, and Data partners. You'll raise the quality of the code around you and get the chance to join the next project like video or catalog enrichment.

Here’s more of what you will get to do: 

- Design, build, and deploy backend services and event-driven pipelines for messaging, notifications, location, and subscriptions

- Improve the reliability, latency, and delivery rates of high-volume messaging and notification systems, including retries, rate limiting, and frequency capping

- Integrate with and operate third-party platforms such as Braze, Amazon Pinpoint, Apple and Google push services, and app store billing

- Own features end-to-end: plan, design, develop, deploy, measure, and iterate

- Break down complex engineering problems into achievable tasks and deliver them within committed timeframes

- Work collaboratively with cross-functional teams (Product, Design, Data Science, Marketing, and iOS, Android, and web engineers) to design and implement new features

- Contribute to A/B tests and use experimentation results to decide what ships

- Actively participate in code reviews and enforce good patterns, testing, and edge-case handling

- Coach and mentor junior team members, new hires, and interns

- Create shared components, utilities, and services that improve team velocity across the stack

- Maintain and improve the runbooks, alerting, and monitoring for the features you ship

- Participate in a reasonable on-call rotation with the rest of the team

- Use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini, and similar) to increase your daily development velocity and code quality

- Become a subject matter expert in one or more of the team's sub-domains: messaging, notifications and campaigns, location, or subscriptions and promotions

You’ll thrive in this role if you have: 

- 2+ years of professional software engineering experience

- Demonstrated ability to own the delivery of multiple features end-to-end (plan, design, develop, and deploy) with high efficiency, including breaking down engineering problems into achievable tasks

- Strong coding skills in Java, with a working understanding of microservices and distributed-systems fundamentals

- Good knowledge of data structures and object-oriented design

- Working knowledge of asynchronous, event-driven systems (queues, pub/sub, or streams), including retries and idempotent processing

- Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (Claude Code or similar) in a real engineering workflow, and a point of view on when they help and when they don't

- A habit of following good coding patterns, writing appropriate tests, considering trade-offs, and seeking out edge cases

- Comfortable giving and receiving feedback in code reviews

- A bias toward shipping, learning from production, and iterating quickly

- An insatiable desire and ability to learn

- BS or MS in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience

Helpful, but not required: 

- Fluency in another modern object-oriented programming language

- Experience with TypeScript and Node.js

- Experience with Agile development

- Experience building and integrating with REST APIs

- Experience with AWS services such as DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, Lambda, and ElastiCache (Redis)

- Experience with notification and engagement platforms (Braze, Amazon Pinpoint, APNs, FCM) or in-app subscription billing (App Store, Google Play)

- Experience with stream processing frameworks such as Apache Flink or Kafka Streams

- Experience with A/B testing platforms (Statsig, LaunchDarkly, Optimizely) and analytics warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake)

- Experience consuming or integrating LLM-based APIs (e.g., Bedrock, Vertex AI, OpenAI)

- Familiarity with Kubernetes, Helm, and CI/CD pipelines

title: Staff Software Engineer, Ecosystem
description:
Headquarters: United States

URL: https://joinblvd.com 

Who is Boulevard? 

Boulevard provides the first and only client experience platform for appointment-based, self-care businesses. We empower our customers to give their clients more of the magical moments that matter most.

Before launching in 2016, our founders spent months interviewing salon managers and working behind front desks to understand their pain points so we could design a modern, user-friendly platform that meets the unique needs of their business. Our roots may be in hair salons, but we are built for the broader self-care industry, including many types of salons, spas, medspa, barbershops, and more. Our technology not only helps our customers survive but thrive. Take a look at how we (and YOU) can make that happen . 

We have an insatiable curiosity and embrace experimentation. We believe that simple solutions require the most sophistication, and we design each and every detail to maximize potential, power, and impact. Do our values match? Read through our story and what we value the most .

Our team values and celebrates our diverse backgrounds. Being open about who we are and what we do allows us to do the best work of our lives. We believe in equal opportunity for all, and you should too.

Come do the best work of your life at Boulevard. 

Boulevard customers are passionate about what they do. Their needs are nuanced and critical, and they rely on us to stand alongside them so they can focus on what they do best. As a Staff Software Engineer on the Ecosystem team, you’ll set the technical direction for Boulevard’s external developer platform and its app and integrations ecosystem, then work across teams to make it real.

This is a green field opportunity. You’ll shape the API platform, the partner experience, and the foundations partners and customers depend on, including API security, identity and access, audit trails, and eventing infrastructure. It’s an individual contributor role with wide influence: you won’t manage people, you’ll lead through technical judgment, clear communication, and trust, working closely with Engineering, Product Management, Design, Partnerships, and Product Marketing. We’re small enough that your work is visible every day.

What you’ll do here: 

- Set the technical strategy for Boulevard’s API and app ecosystem, making sure it supports company goals and partner needs.

- Work across engineering teams to align on direction and drive the right implementation, without formal authority over those teams.

- Lead platform-level changes that cross team boundaries: gain agreement, plan the rollout, and see the work through.

- Find the gaps between what the platform provides and what business priorities require, and turn them into clear, scoped, prioritized proposals.

- Learn what partners and integrators need and bring those needs into the platform roadmap.

- Write and review design documents and architecture decisions, explaining trade-offs and risks to technical and non-technical audiences.

- Write code and ship high-impact work, setting the standard for quality, observability, and security.

- Mentor engineers through design reviews, code reviews, and coaching, and remove blockers so teammates can do their best work.

- Define and monitor system health metrics for the API platform, address technical debt before it affects reliability or performance, and help guide incidents from response to resolution and improvement.

What you’ll need to thrive: 

- Experience as a Staff-level or senior engineer who has led large, cross-team technical initiatives.

- Experience building and scaling external-facing API products. GraphQL experience is strongly preferred.

- Experience building and maintaining integrations with third-party APIs.

- Experience designing and operating systems at scale, including enterprise-grade systems.

- Strong proficiency in at least one programming language, such as Python, Java, Go, or Elixir. Elixir experience is a bonus, not a requirement.

- Influence without authority and sound technical judgment: you gain alignment through clear reasoning and trust, and you anticipate scale, maintenance, and operational cost.

- Business and partner awareness, and clear communication: you connect technical decisions to business priorities and partner needs, and adapt your message to your audience.

- A mentor’s mindset, ownership, and forward thinking: you help other engineers grow, move work forward when the path is unclear, state risks openly, and set long-term direction while delivering value in the short term.

- A plus: experience with multi-tenant SaaS platforms.

How we’ll take care of you: 

At Boulevard, we work hard to structure compensation in a way that balances internal equity with local market competitiveness, and we're happy to share a good-faith estimate of the base salary range for this role. For U.S. based candidates, the anticipated base salary range is $193,900 - 225,000 per year. In addition to this base compensation, this role may be eligible to participate in a variable compensation program. Final compensation will vary based on a variety of factors which include but are not limited to applicable experience, location, and final leveling.

How we take care of our team

Our business is deeply immersed in an industry that’s centered around helping people feel their best, so we know that taking care of yourself isn’t selfish; it’s essential. That’s why our culture pairs high standards with genuine care. We don't glorify burnout or wear ‘always on’ as a badge of honor. Instead, we’ve created benefits designed to support you inside and outside of work, so you can bring your best self to both.

Here’s how we support you:

- Competitive base pay and performance bonus eligibility because you deserve to be rewarded for your impact.

- Equity participation for all full-time employees because we believe the people helping build Boulevard should share in our long-term success.

- Comprehensive medical coverage with up to 100% employee premium coverage and 75% dependent coverage to help take care of you and your loved ones.

- An annual $1,200 HSA employer contribution for eligible plans to help support healthcare costs and future planning.

- 100% covered dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, ensuring you stay healthy, protected, and ready for whatever life brings.

- 12 weeks of fully paid U.S. parental leave supporting all new parents equally as they take the time to bond, adjust, and be present when welcoming a new family member.

- Flexible paid time off, plus 10 U.S. company holidays, where you are encouraged to rest, recharge, and take the time you need, guilt-free. 

- Fully remote with support, including a $200 home office setup allowance and a $50 monthly WFH reimbursement so your workspace is set up for success. 

- $200 quarterly Boulevard Bucks to prioritize your well-being and stay connected to the industry we serve.

- And other perks like One Medical membership and Employee Assistant Program.

To learn how Boulevard collects, uses, and protects personal information related to candidates and employees, please review our Boulevard Employee & Personnel Privacy Notice .

Boulevard Labs, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to hiring a diverse workforce and sustaining an inclusive culture. All employment decisions at Boulevard Labs, Inc. are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law. 

Outside Employment Disclosure 
Boulevard serves the beauty, wellness, and self-care industry, and many of our employees have access to our customers' business and client data. Because of that, we ask all candidates to disclose any concurrent employment, self-employment, ownership interest, or advisory role during the hiring process, including the company name and industry. Disclosure is a normal part of our process and is not by itself a barrier to being hired. Employees in Tier 1 Restricted Roles may not hold concurrent employment, ownership, or an advisory role with a beauty, wellness, self-care, or med-spa business, or with a company that competes with Boulevard. If you currently hold such a role, you are still welcome to apply — please raise it early with your recruiter so we can talk it through. 

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/boulevard-staff-software-engineer-ecosystem

title: Cardog | Toronto, Canada or REMOTE | Full-time
description:
Cardog | Toronto, Canada or REMOTE | Full-time
https://cardog.app/careers We're the system of record for the Canadian vehicle: raw automotive data turned into facts that can be checked. Our open-source VIN decoder sits underneath a government vehicle registry. Some of what's interesting: - A government registry, a manufacturer's own filing, a listing site and an insurance record will describe the same truck four different ways, and nothing in any of those files says they're the same truck. Reconciling that, for every vehicle in the country, in a way that holds up when a regulator asks how you know, is most of the data work. - Seventeen characters on a door frame encode manufacturer, plant, model year and build attributes — badly, inconsistently, and differently per manufacturer. Public reference data covers some of it. The rest gets worked out from filings, recall documents, and patterns inferred across millions of vehicles. - We read vehicles directly over OBD-II now. Forty modules answered on a recent Hyundai, each reporting its own part number and installed software version. Nothing downstream of the VIN moves when a module is reflashed, so no registration, history report or dealer system knows what software is actually in a car. Hiring: VIN Decode Engineer, Data Platform Engineer, Infrastructure Engineer, Founding Engineer (dealer platform). TypeScript, Postgres, Cloudflare Workers. Full descriptions and apply: https://cardog.app/careers

About DrFirst

For 25 years, DrFirst has empowered providers and patients to achieve better health through intelligent medication management. We improve healthcare workflows and help patients start and stay on therapy with end-to-end solutions that enhance prescription access, affordability, and adherence. Our solutions help 100 million patients a year and are used by more than 420,000 prescribers, 71,000 pharmacies, 270 EHRs and health information systems, and over 2,000 hospitals in the U.S. This is a great opportunity to be a part of a successful Healthcare IT company experiencing significant growth. If you get excited about stretching yourself in new ways, developing yourself to your fullest potential, and care about working with smart colleagues, we want to talk to you!

Position Overview

DrFirst is hiring a Senior Software Engineer for the eRx Enterprise and Gadget team. Your first focus is Gadget, our pharmacy agent. Over time you will extend your work into Rcopia, our ePrescribing platform, on Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances (EPCS) and Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) workflows.

You will build cloud native, high performance services for an ePrescribing collaboration platform. The platform connects providers, patients, payers, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical companies in real time. You will design systems built for high load, with self healing, auto scaling, and full observability.

You bring strong judgment about AI. You know when AI speeds up delivery and when AI produces weak code. You apply AI to raise code quality, performance, and design standards across the team, and you solve real problems for the pharmacies and prescribers who rely on our platform.

What You Will Work On

- Build and improve Gadget, the DrFirst pharmacy agent, from design through production.
- Contribute to Rcopia EPCS and PDMP capabilities as the team roadmap expands.
- Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain secure, scalable Java integration solutions.
- Build cloud native microservices on AWS with auto scaling, fault tolerance, high availability, and self healing.
- Develop and maintain integrations with major EHR platforms, including athenaOne, Epic, Oracle Health, Greenway, AdvancedMD, eMDs, and ModMed, using HL7, FHIR, web services, APIs, and Mirth Connect.
- Build and maintain event driven architectures with Apache Kafka for reliable, efficient service communication.
- Deliver high throughput and low latency across large, distributed platforms.
- Partner with DevOps on CI/CD pipelines that automate testing, deployment, and monitoring.
- Design AI powered automation frameworks for faster development cycles and automated regression testing.
- Decide where AI adds value in the codebase and where human design must lead. Set review standards for AI assisted code.
- Monitor, diagnose, and resolve performance issues with observability tools and logs.
- Follow and enforce secure coding practices. Take part in security audits and reviews.
- Lead code reviews, mentor junior developers, and contribute to architecture decisions.
- Track industry trends and improve system performance, resilience, and developer productivity.

Qualifications

Required

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related discipline.
- 5+ years of hands on Java development with deep knowledge of object oriented design and the Spring Framework, including Spring Boot and Spring Cloud.
- 3+ years designing and building cloud native applications on AWS, including S3, Valkey, Lambda, RDS, and EKS or ECS.
- 3+ years with distributed messaging systems such as Apache Kafka, with a solid grasp of event streaming.
- Proven record building and integrating large scale, high performance, distributed systems with fault tolerance, scalability, and low latency.
- AI first mindset, with daily hands on use of AI tools such as Claude and GitHub Copilot for coding, testing, debugging, and documentation.
- Clear judgment on when and where AI improves engineering outcomes, and a record of keeping AI generated code from lowering quality, performance, or design.
- Proficiency building and consuming RESTful APIs with JSON and XML.
- Strong experience with relational or NoSQL databases, including schema design, performance tuning, and query optimization.
- Hands on experience with CI/CD pipelines and tools such as GitLab CI and Jenkins.
- Solid knowledge of application and data security, including authentication, authorization, and data protection.
- Self motivated. You work well on your own in a fast paced, agile environment.
- Fast learner who adapts to new technologies, teams, and environments.
- Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with a proactive, solution oriented approach.

Preferred

- Experience building AI agents, LLM integrations, or agentic workflows in production.
- Experience with large scale, mission critical systems in finance, brokerage, trading, or credit card processing, especially systems requiring low latency, high throughput, and high availability.
- Experience with ePrescribing, EPCS, PDMP, NCPDP SCRIPT, or pharmacy systems.
- Familiarity with front end technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).

Physical Requirements

- Primarily desk work in a remote, U.S. based setting.
- Extended periods of computer use.

We’re a fully remote company with a global footprint across 20+ countries. We’re growing, profitable, employee-owned, and have no dependence on outside funding. We’re obsessed with computers, programming, big data, databases, compilers, hardware, math, data science, and the internet. Does this sound like you? Please apply to join our team. Our codebase is friendly to new contributors. You’ll have a fully functional development environment within hours through full automation and will be pushing commits on your first day. Deployments to production happen multiple times per day and finish in under two minutes.Effectively all of our codebase is written in Python, Rust, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Nix. The core technologies you’ll need familiarity with to be productive are Python, PostgreSQL, Linux, and Git. We operate at a larger scale than typical startups. We run two datacenters with high-performance servers we’ve built ourselves, capable of handling the volumes of data we process. We’ve implemented our own distributed file system, perform full-scale web crawls, and download and run static analysis on the entire universe of published Android APKs and iOS IPAs. Unlike a typical startup where you might spend half your time in meetings and the other half fixing Jira tickets, at MixRank you’ll challenge yourself with difficult technical problems that help you grow as an individual. We’re continuously hiring for the positions below; these aren’t singular roles that close once filled. Our philosophy is that the candidate is more important than the position. For each new member of the team, we design a custom role and responsibilities around their interests.
Other companies may create a long list of specific requirements with the expectation that you’ll exactly replace someone on the team or fit a role defined by committee. MixRank is more pragmatic: we first get excited about bringing a unique individual onto the team, then figure out the best way to support their specific talents. Junior Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time We’re looking for remote junior engineers with 0–3 years of professional software experience and 5+ years of curiosity exploring computers, programming, and technical hobby projects. This is an open-ended entry role with mentorship and diverse opportunities to work across all areas of our product: databases, distributed systems, infrastructure and tooling, data analysis, machine learning, frontend/backend web development, APIs, data mining, data modeling, and more. To stand out, please highlight what makes you unique: passion for computing, curiosity and side projects, work ethic, niche research, or anything else that shows how you think and build. Ideally, you’ve already graduated. But if you still have one or more years left of school, please feel free to apply anyway. If you’re the right fit for the team, we’ll figure out a way to accommodate your schedule. We’ll tailor the role to the subset of areas that best match your interests. Beneficial experience includes PostgreSQL, Python, Rust, Linux, TypeScript, Nix, frontend/backend web development, and data mining. title: Senior Data Engineers
description:
Headquarters: United States

URL: https://jobs.workable.com/company/sx6tzFKwyUTPcquYzQkRFu/jobs-at-movement-labs 

Movement Labs is an incubator and consulting firm that uses technology, data, and experimentation to stop fascism and build progressive power. We help progressives win and defeat MAGA extremists through year-round work grounded in research and real-world testing. Our team partners with leading advocacy groups, grassroots organizers, and electoral campaigns to develop innovative tactics, win elections, and shift power for the long term.

As the R&D powerhouse for the progressive movement, we’ve run over 100 randomized control trials (RCTs) on voter behavior and helped hundreds of organizations increase their impact. We work hard, and the environment evolves rapidly. We are adaptable, nimble, and shift quickly as needed to meet the moment. We are looking for candidates that thrive in this type of environment.

We are looking for 2 roles, Senior and Mid-level Data Engineers to join the Tech department. You will be a part of an 8-person data engineering team, and will have a lot of ownership and ability to make an impact. You’ll work cross-functionally in a collaborative, startup-like environment. 

What the work looks like for our data team: 

- Design and implement scalable data architecture for targeting and engagement
- Serve as technical partner to program teams
- Extend our foundational datasets to facilitate new outreach strategies
- Load-test our systems to prepare for elections 
- Maintain key datasets for polling images and precinct cross-matching
- Develop standardized experimental frameworks for testing campaign effectiveness
- Build AI tooling that makes our own team faster — QC agents for data deliveries, the evals to trust them, and context systems that keep our repos self-documenting
Our data team’s work mixes greenfield builds, pragmatic plumbing, incident response, and operational work. The relative mix shifts with the political calendar.

This role is fully remote. This position has an initial term of six (6) months beginning on the employee's start date.

Responsibilities - Shape the pipelines and integrations feeding our RCT platform and our foundational voter datasets: the APIs, replication, federation layers, experiment randomization, and the failure modes that come with running data systems for hundreds of partner organizations on a non-negotiable political calendar
- Extend our data platform and orchestration layer, and optimize it for cost, runtime, and reliability so it holds up during the elections, with millions of outreach attempts
- Lead projects that span multiple systems and teams — scoping, designing, and driving them to real milestones
- Hold the bar on quality — test and validate your own work, review teammates' code, and mentor through that review
- Document and communicate — make your systems understandable to teammates, stakeholders, and non-engineers
- Rotate through on-call and rapid response, including evenings and weekends during high-stakes moments like election cycles

- Passionate about progressive politics and leveraging data, technology, organizing and research to build political power
- 3-6+ years of experience (Senior or Mid-level) in designing, building, and operating production data pipelines and integrations
- Strong proficiency in SQL and Python
- Experience building production software across a modern data stack — cloud data warehouses (BigQuery or similar), a transformation framework like dbt, and an orchestrator like Dagster or Airflow
- A track record of leading technical work across multiple systems or teams, and scoping ambiguous problems end-to-end
- Sound judgment about when to refactor, when to ship pragmatically, and how to leave systems better than you found them
- Strong written communication — you document what you build and can explain complex systems to non-engineers
- Genuine commitment to the mission of stopping fascism and building progressive power, and comfort operating on a political calendar

Nice to Have:

- Experience in the progressive, political, advocacy, or nonprofit sector — including awareness of c3/c4/PAC boundaries and the sensitivities of political and voter data
- Familiarity with election results, voter file data, and the tools campaigns use to organize, text, and contact voters
- Experience on Google Cloud Platform 
- Experience in on-call rotations and mentoring less-experienced engineers
We’re looking for candidates with a wide range of skills and experience. If you’re excited about the job, even if you don’t match all the characteristics, we encourage you to apply. 

- Base salary of $90,000-$150,000
- Excellent health, dental, and vision benefits, 401(k) matching, and unlimited Paid Time Off 
- Remote first culture with teammates all around the country.
- This position has an initial term of six (6) months beginning on the employee's start date. We love to keep top performers if possible.

Applications may be reviewed earlier on a rolling basis so it benefits candidates to apply as soon as possible. The application process includes a phone screen, an exercise, and a full interview with the hiring manager. Due to the nature of our work, the process is moving quickly, and we hope candidates will start as soon as possible. Applicants must be legally eligible to work in the United States. We are not able to provide sponsorship at this time.

Movement Labs is an equal opportunity employer with a commitment to economic and social justice. Women, people of color, LGBTQ people, people with disabilities, and members of other historically disenfranchised populations are strongly encouraged to apply. If you require accommodations as part of the hiring process, please contact careers@movementlabs.com.

Applications are reviewed by our hiring team—not automated systems. Our hiring process may include AI-assisted analysis of candidate materials, however, hiring decisions are made by human reviewers.
